std:iterator.name: Iterator
IteratorResult
std:iterator.signature: type IteratorResult<T> = { done: false; value: T } | { done: true }

done.documentation:
Reports whether advancement found no item. false permits reading value; true has no value payload. It is a copied boolean and does not advance or mutate the iterator.

Example: Iterator.from([2]).next().done returns false.

Ownership: reading the flag borrows the result.

value.documentation:
Contains the yielded owned item only when done is false. Narrow the result by checking done before reading value; accessing value on the done alternative is rejected.

Example: const step=Iterator.from([2]).next(); if(!step.done){console.log(step.value);} prints 2.

Ownership: moving value transfers the item; borrowing it keeps the result owner alive.

std:url.name: Url
std:url.documentation:
A parsed, independently owned URL with checked computed properties. parseUrl and resolveUrl return Result; malformed input returns UrlError. Components normalize using the URL backend, including IDNA hosts and default ports. Read getters without reparsing. Write properties with plain assignment; invalid writes throw UrlError. origin is read-only. No constructor defaults or network/DNS lookup are involved. Some backend parsing differences from the URL Standard are documented in the reference.

```tsrust
const value = unwrap(parseUrl('https://EXAMPLE.com:443/a/../b'));
console.log(value.href); // https://example.com/b
```

Ownership: one owner; clone makes independent storage. Component StringView values borrow it until their last use.

examples.source:
import { parseUrl } from 'std:url';
function main() { const value=unwrap(parseUrl('https://EXAMPLE.com:443/a/../b'));console.log(value.href); }

std:url.name: SearchParams
std:url.documentation:
An owned ordered list of decoded query name/value pairs, including duplicates. Create with parseQuery or searchParams(url). Parsing uses form encoding: plus means space, malformed percent escapes remain literal, and invalid decoded UTF-8 is replaced. get borrows the first value; getAll and entries copy independent snapshots. Mutators preserve the documented duplicate order. No URL is modified until setSearchParams is called.

```tsrust
const params = parseQuery('x=1&x=2');
console.log(params.getAll('x').join(',')); // 1,2
```

Ownership: independent owner; clone copies the list. A borrowed get result prevents mutation until its last use.

examples.source:
import { parseQuery } from 'std:url';
function main() { const params=parseQuery('x=1&x=2');console.log(params.getAll('x').join(',')); }

std:url.name: StringView
std:url.documentation:
A scoped read-only view of valid UTF-8 text. URL properties and SearchParams.get return views without copying substrings. Read length or use the supported string inspection methods; String(view) creates independent owned text. This export is the shared StringView identity.

```tsrust

console.log(value.pathname.length); // 2
```

Ownership: borrows the originating owner. It cannot escape that owner's lifetime or remain live across its mutation.

Url.name: href
Url.documentation:
Full canonical URL serialization, including any credentials.

A plain property assignment accepts string and throws UrlError if rejected. The receiver and RHS evaluate once in ordinary assignment order. Invalid checks precede mutation. Compound/update assignment is unsupported.

```tsrust
const value = unwrap(parseUrl('https://u:secret@example.com:8080/a?q=1#f'));
console.log(value.href); // https://u:secret@example.com:8080/a?q=1#f
```

Ownership: the getter returns a scoped StringView borrowing the whole URL. Use String(view) for independent text. A live view prevents any URL mutation or transfer. Standalone property assignment moves an owned string RHS as ordinary assignment does; clone(text) retains an independent caller value.

function main() { const value=unwrap(parseUrl('https://u:secret@example.com:8080/a?q=1#f'));console.log(value.href); }

std:sql.name: Pool
Transaction
Row
SqlError
Cursor
std:sql.documentation:
An owned row cursor borrowing its Pool. Obtain it with await db.cursor(sql, parameters); await cursor.next() yields one owned Row or undefined at EOF. Close or drop it to release its pending result stream. This is client-side row streaming, not a named server cursor or a transaction snapshot.

```tsrust
const cursor = await db.cursor('SELECT 1 AS value');
const row = await cursor.next(); // Row with value 1
cursor.close();
```

Ownership: cannot clone or outlive its pool. Each pending next() exclusively borrows the cursor.

SqlPool.name: query
SqlPool.signature: query(sql: string, parameters?: (int | number | boolean | string | null | Bytes)[]): Task<Row[]>

parameters.label: sql: string
parameters.documentation: One SQL statement. Bind values rather than interpolating input. Use aliases for duplicate column names. Transaction/session control SQL is unsupported.

parameters.label: parameters?: (int | number | boolean | string | null | Bytes)[]
parameters.documentation: Positional values, default []. int is signed 64-bit; number must be finite; Bytes binds a blob. When driver metadata requests binary32 REAL, narrowing rejects precision loss with precision and overflow with range. Server-side implicit casts can still round; use std:numeric.toFloat32 before binding to a binary32 column when metadata does not expose its width. Use driver-compatible column types and explicit SQL casts where needed. Omit or pass undefined to use the default.

SqlPool.documentation:
Returns all result rows as owned values. All rows are materialized; use Pool.cursor() for row-at-a-time consumption. Uses one prepared SQL statement and positional parameter binding. Missing/extra parameters and database failures throw SqlError at await. SQL text remains driver-specific. No string escaping or identifier sanitization is performed.  Omitting parameters or passing undefined binds no values.

```tsrust
const rows = await db.query('SELECT id, name FROM people');
```

SQL may perform writes using a returning clause.

Ownership: borrows the pool for reading until the operation finishes or is dropped. Arguments evaluate when the Task is created. Owned SQL text and parameter arrays move into it; use clone when reuse is needed.

SqlPool.documentation:
Returns the affected row count; returned result columns are discarded. Uses one prepared SQL statement and positional parameter binding. Missing/extra parameters and database failures throw SqlError at await. SQL text remains driver-specific. No string escaping or identifier sanitization is performed.  Omitting parameters or passing undefined binds no values.

```tsrust

```

Ownership: borrows the pool for reading until the operation finishes or is dropped. Arguments evaluate when the Task is created. Owned SQL text and parameter arrays move into it; use clone when reuse is needed.

SqlPool.name: migrate

parameters.label: directory: string
parameters.documentation: Trusted migration directory, relative to the process working directory or absolute. Ship these files with your service. Direct .sql files must have unique positive signed-64-bit VERSION_description.sql names.

SqlPool.documentation:
Applies pending migrations from `directory` in version order and checks the checksums of those already applied. Running it again with the same files does nothing. Progress is recorded in the `_sqlx_migrations` table; PostgreSQL and MySQL take a lock, so run migrations from one deployment step, not while serving requests.

Only `.sql` files directly in the directory are read. Empty files, duplicate or non-positive versions, `.up`/`.down` files and `-- no-transaction` files throw `migration-source`. In-memory SQLite databases are unsupported. An applied file that is missing or changed throws `migration-drift`; an unfinished MySQL migration throws `migration-dirty`; a failing migration throws `migration-failed`. PostgreSQL and SQLite roll back a failed migration; MySQL schema changes may be left half applied.

```tsrust
await pool.migrate('examples/sql-migrations/migrations');
await pool.migrate('examples/sql-migrations/migrations'); // already applied
```

Checksums detect edited migration files, not schema changes made by hand. There are no down migrations or automatic repair, and the SQL is not translated between databases. Scripts must not change transactions or the migration table.

Ownership: borrows the pool until it finishes.

SqlPool.name: begin
close
SqlPool.documentation:
Closes the pool when awaited and waits for connections to finish cleanup. Takes no arguments. Returns no value.

```tsrust
await db.close();
```

Ownership: consumes the pool immediately when creating the Task. Live operation or transaction borrows prevent close; dropping the Task still triggers pool cleanup.

SqlPool.signature: cursor(sql: string, parameters?: (int | number | boolean | string | null | Bytes)[]): Task<Cursor>

parameters.label: sql: string
parameters.documentation: One SQL statement. Bind values rather than interpolating input. Use aliases for duplicate column names. Transaction/session control SQL is unsupported.

parameters.label: parameters?: (int | number | boolean | string | null | Bytes)[]
parameters.documentation: Positional values, default []. int is signed 64-bit; number must be finite; Bytes binds a blob. When driver metadata requests binary32 REAL, narrowing rejects precision loss with precision and overflow with range. Server-side implicit casts can still round; use std:numeric.toFloat32 before binding to a binary32 column when metadata does not expose its width. Use driver-compatible column types and explicit SQL casts where needed. Omit or pass undefined to use the default.

SqlPool.documentation:
Runs a query and returns a cursor that streams rows instead of collecting them all. Parameters work as in `query()` (default `[]`). The query starts on the first `next()`; errors can be thrown there too. Rows come in database order, so use `ORDER BY` when order matters.

Writes made by the query (for example with `RETURNING`) are not undone by closing the cursor. Multiple statements and session commands are rejected, and transactions have no cursor. Omitting parameters or passing undefined binds no values.

```tsrust
const cursor = await db.cursor('SELECT 1 AS value');
const row = await cursor.next(); // one Row
cursor.close();
```

Ownership: the cursor borrows the pool until closed or dropped.

SqlTransaction.signature: query(sql: string, parameters?: (int | number | boolean | string | null | Bytes)[]): Task<Row[]>

parameters.label: sql: string
parameters.documentation: One SQL statement. Bind values rather than interpolating input. Use aliases for duplicate column names. Transaction/session control SQL is unsupported.

SqlTransaction.documentation:
Runs a query in the transaction and returns all rows. Parameters bind positionally; the SQL text is not escaped or rewritten. Schema changes and transaction or session commands are rejected. Omitting parameters or passing undefined binds no values.

```tsrust
const rows = await transaction.query('SELECT id, name FROM people');
```

A wrong parameter count or a database error throws `SqlError` when awaited. Any failure or cancellation rolls the transaction back and makes it inactive. The SQL may write and return rows with `RETURNING`.

Ownership: borrows the transaction until the query finishes; the SQL and parameters move into the task.

parameters.label: parameters?: (int | number | boolean | string | null | Bytes)[]
parameters.documentation: Positional values, default []. int is signed 64-bit; number must be finite; Bytes binds a blob. When driver metadata requests binary32 REAL, narrowing rejects precision loss with precision and overflow with range. Server-side implicit casts can still round; use std:numeric.toFloat32 before binding to a binary32 column when metadata does not expose its width. Use driver-compatible column types and explicit SQL casts where needed. Omit or pass undefined to use the default.

SqlTransaction.documentation:
Returns the affected row count; returned result columns are discarded. Uses one prepared SQL statement and positional parameter binding. Missing/extra parameters and database failures throw SqlError at await. SQL text remains driver-specific. No string escaping or identifier sanitization is performed. Transaction DDL and raw transaction/session commands are rejected.  Omitting parameters or passing undefined binds no values.

```tsrust
const removed = await transaction.execute('DELETE FROM people WHERE id = ?', [1]); // 1 if found
```

A database/parameter failure or cancellation schedules rollback and makes the transaction inactive. Cleanup may wait for an in-flight statement.

Ownership: borrows the transaction exclusively until the operation finishes or is dropped. Arguments evaluate when the Task is created. Owned SQL text and parameter arrays move into it; use clone when reuse is needed.

SqlTransaction.name: commit
SqlTransaction.documentation:
Commits changes. Takes no arguments; returns no value. Database failures throw SqlError at await. A cancelled or disconnected commit may have reached the server: do not retry a non-idempotent transaction blindly.

```tsrust
await transaction.commit();
```

Ownership: consumes the transaction. Dropping an unfinished transaction schedules rollback; the pool connection is not reused before cleanup.

SqlTransaction.name: rollback
SqlTransaction.documentation:

```tsrust

```

Ownership: consumes the transaction. Dropping an unfinished transaction schedules rollback; the pool connection is not reused before cleanup.

```tsrust
unwrap(db.close()); // db is no longer usable
```

Ownership: consumes the connection. Cannot close while statements or a transaction borrow it; scope exit also closes automatically.

SqliteTransaction.name: commit

Commits all changes in this transaction. Deferred constraint or lock failures return SqliteError and trigger rollback. If SQLite already aborted the transaction, returns transaction-ended. No arguments or success value.

```tsrust
unwrap(tx.commit());
```

Ownership: consumes the transaction and releases its exclusive connection borrow. All its statements must be released first.

SqliteTransaction.name: rollback
SqliteTransaction.documentation:

```tsrust
unwrap(tx.rollback());
```

Ownership: consumes the transaction. All statements must be released first. Scope exit and errors also roll back automatically.

SqliteStatement.name: execute
SqliteStatement.signature: execute(parameters?: (int | number | string | null | Bytes)[]): Result<int, SqliteError>

parameters.label: parameters?: (int | number | string | null | Bytes)[]
parameters.documentation: parameters is an optional array of int | number | string | null | Bytes; omitted or undefined uses []. Bindings follow SQLite parameter indexes (prefer ?1, ?2). Supply exactly the placeholder count on every call; prior values are never reused. int preserves signed 64-bit INTEGER; finite number binds REAL; string binds UTF-8 TEXT, Bytes binds BLOB and null binds SQL NULL. No string interpolation. Arrays and byte buffers are read, not consumed.

SqliteStatement.documentation:
Runs a prepared statement that returns no rows and gives SQLite's change count: rows affected by INSERT, UPDATE or DELETE, not counting triggers. Other statements may report the previous count. SELECT and RETURNING are rejected; use `query`.

@param parameters - Values for the placeholders (prefer `?1`, `?2`), exactly one per placeholder on every call; default `[]`. `int` binds INTEGER, `number` REAL, `string` TEXT, `Bytes` BLOB and `null` NULL. Values are never interpolated into the SQL text.

```tsrust
unwrap(insert.execute([1, 'Ada'])); // 1 inserted row
```

Failure returns `SqliteError`.

Ownership: borrows the parameters for the call.

SqliteStatement.documentation:
Runs a read-only prepared statement and returns all rows (`[]` if none). Use `LIMIT` for large results. Writes, duplicate column names (use `AS` aliases) and invalid UTF-8 text are rejected.

@param parameters - Values for the placeholders (prefer `?1`, `?2`), exactly one per placeholder on every call; default `[]`. `int` binds INTEGER, `number` REAL, `string` TEXT, `Bytes` BLOB and `null` NULL. Values are never interpolated into the SQL text.

```tsrust
const rows = unwrap(select.query([1]));
```

Failure returns `SqliteError`.

Ownership: rows own their values and outlive the statement.


Ownership: consumes the statement and releases its connection/transaction borrow. Scope exit finalizes automatically.

std:futures.name: delay

parameters.label: milliseconds: int
parameters.documentation: Creates a lazy timer. Awaiting waits without blocking a worker thread. milliseconds is an integer from zero through the target-representable timer deadline; zero imposes no positive delay. Invalid values throw AsyncError code range when awaited. No receiver mutation.

std:futures.documentation:
Creates a lazy timer. Awaiting waits without blocking a worker thread. milliseconds is an integer from zero through the target-representable timer deadline; zero imposes no positive delay. Invalid values throw AsyncError code range when awaited. No receiver mutation.

```tsrust
await delay(10); // waits at least 10 ms
```

Ownership: uniquely owned task; await once or transfer it.

Renamed imports retain this operation's contract. Call the imported operation directly; storing it as a function value is unsupported. The concrete Task returned by the call can be stored or forwarded.

examples.source: import {delay} from 'std:futures'; async function main():Task<void>{await delay(1); console.log('ready');}

std:futures.name: yield
std:futures.documentation:
Gives the scheduler a chance to run other ready tasks when awaited. Resumes without a fixed delay; another task is not guaranteed to run first. Acts on the task executing await; it cannot pause another job or choose which task runs next. Calling yield() alone does nothing until awaited. Usually unnecessary when already awaiting timers or channel operations. Takes no arguments and returns no value. No receiver mutation or ordinary failures.

```tsrust
await yield(); // resume after yielding to the scheduler
```

Ownership: consumes the task once.

Renamed imports retain this operation's contract. Call the imported operation directly; storing it as a function value is unsupported. The concrete Task returned by the call can be stored or forwarded.

std:futures.name: race

parameters.label: inputs: (Task<T> | Job<T, E>)[]
parameters.documentation: Creates a lazy race over an owned array. Lazy inputs begin together when awaited; started jobs continue running. First completion, including failure, wins. Ready ties prefer input order. Cancels remaining work and waits for cleanup before returning. Empty input throws AsyncError code empty. Every input must have the same result type. Worker failures retain their typed cause. No input array mutation is visible after transfer.

std:futures.documentation:
Creates a lazy race over an owned array. Lazy inputs begin together when awaited; started jobs continue running. First completion, including failure, wins. Ready ties prefer input order. Cancels remaining work and waits for cleanup before returning. Empty input throws AsyncError code empty. Every input must have the same result type. Mix tasks and jobs in an array literal at the call; stored arrays hold one input type. Worker failures retain their typed cause. No input array mutation is visible after transfer.

```tsrust
const result = await race([slow(), fast().start()]);
```

Ownership: consumes the array and every input. Started-job settlement obligations remain active inside the returned task. Cancelling a parent drains its children.

examples.source: import {race,allSettled} from 'std:futures';async function value(n:int):Task<int>{return n;}async function main():Task<void>{console.log(await race([value(1),value(2)]));const results=await allSettled([value(3),value(4).start()]);for(const result of results){console.log(unwrap(clone(result)));}}

std:futures.name: allSettled

parameters.label: inputs: (Task<T> | Job<T, E>)[]
parameters.documentation: Creates a lazy group that waits for every outcome, including failures, in input order. Lazy inputs begin together when awaited; started jobs continue running. Empty input returns an empty array. All inputs need the same result type. A failure does not cancel siblings. Errors carry code and optional typed cause.

std:futures.documentation:
Creates a lazy group that waits for every outcome, including failures, in input order. Lazy inputs begin together when awaited; started jobs continue running. Empty input returns an empty array. All inputs need the same result type. Mix tasks and jobs in an array literal at the call; stored arrays hold one input type. A failure does not cancel siblings. Errors carry code and optional typed cause.

```tsrust

```

Ownership: consumes inputs and transfers any started-job obligations to the group. Parent cancellation cancels and drains children.

examples.source: import {race,allSettled} from 'std:futures';async function value(n:int):Task<int>{return n;}async function main():Task<void>{console.log(await race([value(1),value(2)]));const results=await allSettled([value(3),value(4).start()]);for(const result of results){console.log(unwrap(clone(result)));}}

std:futures.documentation:
Creates a bounded async channel. capacity is the maximum number of queued messages, positive and within the target backend limit; invalid capacity throws RangeError. const queue = new Channel<int>(2);

examples.source: import {Channel} from 'std:futures';async function main():Task<void>{const queue=new Channel<int>(2);const sender=queue.sender();await sender.send(42);console.log(await queue.receive());queue.close();try{await queue.receive();}catch(error){console.log(error.code);}}

std:futures.documentation:
Runs tasks and jobs together and returns their results in input order. All inputs share one result type; `void` tasks give `void[]`. The first failure throws `AsyncError<E>`, cancels the rest and waits for them to stop.

```tsrust
const values = await all([first(), second().start()]);
```

Call it directly (a renamed import works); `const collect = all` is rejected. Mixing tasks and jobs needs an array literal at the call.

Ownership: consumes the array and every input.

examples.source: import {all} from 'std:futures';async function value(n:int):Task<int>{return n;}async function unit():Task<void>{}async function main():Task<void>{const values=await all([value(2),value(1).start()]);console.log(values[0],values[1]);console.log((await all([unit(),unit()])).length,(await all([])).length);}

std:futures.name: Interval
std:futures.signature: new Interval(periodMs: int, missedTickBehavior?: MissedTickBehavior): Interval

parameters.label: periodMs: int
parameters.documentation: Positive integer milliseconds within the target deadline range; no artificial duration ceiling.

parameters.label: missedTickBehavior?: MissedTickBehavior
parameters.documentation: burst by default; delay shifts the schedule after lateness; skip omits missed ticks.

std:futures.documentation:
Creates a periodic timer on an active async runtime. periodMs must be positive and fit the target timer deadline; invalid periods throw RangeError. Calling outside a runtime throws RuntimeError. missedTickBehavior is burst (default), delay or skip. First tick is immediately ready. burst catches up missed ticks, delay schedules from the late tick, and skip resumes the original schedule after skipped ticks. Timing resolution depends on the platform.

```tsrust
const timer = new Interval(10, 'skip');
await timer.tick(); // first tick is immediate
```

Ownership: unique timer; tick retains an exclusive borrow until completion or disposal.

examples.source: import {Interval,MissedTickBehavior} from 'std:futures';async function main():Task<void>{const policy:MissedTickBehavior='skip';const timer=new Interval(1,policy);await timer.tick();console.log('tick');}

std:futures.name: MissedTickBehavior
std:futures.documentation:
Controls how Interval handles missed ticks. burst is the default and catches up; delay shifts the next deadline from the late tick; skip omits missed ticks and preserves the original schedule. Applies when lateness exceeds the backend timer tolerance.

```tsrust
const timer = new Interval(10, 'burst');
```

Ownership: immutable literal data.

examples.source: import {Interval,MissedTickBehavior} from 'std:futures';async function main():Task<void>{const policy:MissedTickBehavior='skip';const timer=new Interval(1,policy);await timer.tick();console.log('tick');}

std:futures.name: CancellationToken
std:futures.documentation:
Creates an uncancelled cooperative signal. No arguments or runtime is required. share explicitly creates another handle to the same signal; child creates a descendant signal. cancel wakes cancelled waiters and propagates to descendants. Dropping a handle does not cancel it. A child cannot cancel its parent.

```tsrust
const token = new CancellationToken();
token.cancel();
await token.cancelled(); // already ready
```

Ownership: explicit share/child handles; operations borrow the handle.

examples.source: import {CancellationToken} from 'std:futures';async function main():Task<void>{const token=new CancellationToken();const shared=token.share();const child=token.child();child.cancel();console.log(token.isCancelled(),child.isCancelled());shared.cancel();await token.cancelled();console.log(token.isCancelled());}

Creates a lazy send. Awaiting waits for queue capacity without blocking a worker. Consumes one value; closed queues throw SendError<T> code closed with the exact unsent value. Starting this task wraps that error in AsyncError as for other Jobs. A cancelled pending send releases its owned message.

AsyncChannel.name: receive
AsyncChannel.documentation:
Creates a lazy receive. Awaiting waits for one queued message. After close, queued messages drain; an empty closed queue throws AsyncError code closed. No arguments or defaults. Cancelling a pending receive does not consume a message.

```tsrust
const value = await queue.receive();
```

Ownership: task retains a read borrow of the channel.

examples.source: import {Channel} from 'std:futures';async function main():Task<void>{const queue=new Channel<int>(2);const sender=queue.sender();await sender.send(42);console.log(await queue.receive());queue.close();try{await queue.receive();}catch(error){console.log(error.code);}}

AsyncChannel.name: close
AsyncChannel.documentation:
Closes this channel to new sends. Existing queued messages remain receivable; later receives on an empty channel throw closed. Wakes blocked senders. Repeated close is harmless.

```tsrust
queue.close();
```

Ownership: mutably borrows the channel, so outstanding channel-operation loans must finish first.

examples.source: import {Channel} from 'std:futures';async function main():Task<void>{const queue=new Channel<int>(2);const sender=queue.sender();await sender.send(42);console.log(await queue.receive());queue.close();try{await queue.receive();}catch(error){console.log(error.code);}}

AsyncChannel.name: trySend

parameters.label: value: T
parameters.documentation: Owned transferable message; returned intact on full or closed.

AsyncChannel.documentation:
Attempts one send immediately. Success queues the consumed value. Returns full when capacity is exhausted, or closed when this endpoint or its receiver is closed. Both errors retain the original unsent value. Never waits.

```tsrust
unwrap(sender.trySend(7));
```

Ownership: borrows the endpoint and consumes value; the error owns value on failure.

examples.source: import {Channel} from 'std:futures';async function main():Task<void>{const queue=new Channel<int>(1);const sender=queue.sender();unwrap(sender.trySend(7));console.log(unwrap(queue.tryReceive()));sender.close();sender.close();try{await sender.send(9);}catch(error){console.log(error.code,error.value);}queue.close();}

AsyncChannel.name: tryReceive
AsyncChannel.documentation:
Attempts to remove one queued message immediately. Returns empty for an open empty queue and closed for a closed empty queue. Buffered messages remain available after close. Never waits; no arguments.

```tsrust
console.log(unwrap(queue.tryReceive()));
```

Ownership: exclusively borrows the receiver and returns ownership of one message.

examples.source: import {Channel} from 'std:futures';async function main():Task<void>{const queue=new Channel<int>(1);const sender=queue.sender();unwrap(sender.trySend(7));console.log(unwrap(queue.tryReceive()));sender.close();sender.close();try{await sender.send(9);}catch(error){console.log(error.code,error.value);}queue.close();}

AsyncSender.name: send

parameters.label: value: T
parameters.documentation: Creates a lazy send. Awaiting waits for queue capacity without blocking a worker. Consumes one value; closed queues throw SendError<T> code closed retaining value. A cancelled pending send releases its owned message.

AsyncSender.documentation:
Creates a lazy send. Awaiting waits for queue capacity without blocking a worker. Consumes one value; closed queues throw SendError<T> code closed with the exact unsent value. Starting this task wraps that error in AsyncError as for other Jobs. A cancelled pending send releases its owned message.

```tsrust
await queue.send(42);
```

Ownership: task retains a read borrow of the endpoint until completion or disposal.

examples.source: import {Channel} from 'std:futures';async function main():Task<void>{const queue=new Channel<int>(2);const sender=queue.sender();await sender.send(42);console.log(await queue.receive());queue.close();try{await queue.receive();}catch(error){console.log(error.code);}}

parameters.label: value: T
parameters.documentation: Owned transferable message; returned intact on full or closed.

AsyncSender.documentation:
Attempts one send immediately. Success queues the consumed value. Returns full when capacity is exhausted, or closed when this endpoint or its receiver is closed. Both errors retain the original unsent value. Never waits.

```tsrust
unwrap(sender.trySend(7));
```

Ownership: borrows the endpoint and consumes value; the error owns value on failure.

examples.source: import {Channel} from 'std:futures';async function main():Task<void>{const queue=new Channel<int>(1);const sender=queue.sender();unwrap(sender.trySend(7));console.log(unwrap(queue.tryReceive()));sender.close();sender.close();try{await sender.send(9);}catch(error){console.log(error.code,error.value);}queue.close();}

AsyncSender.name: close
AsyncSender.documentation:
Releases only this sending endpoint. Repeated close is harmless. Other senders and the channel remain usable. Future sends through this endpoint return closed with their unsent value. No arguments or return value.

```tsrust
sender.close();
```

Ownership: exclusively borrows this sender; finish its outstanding send loans first.

examples.source: import {Channel} from 'std:futures';async function main():Task<void>{const queue=new Channel<int>(1);const sender=queue.sender();unwrap(sender.trySend(7));console.log(unwrap(queue.tryReceive()));sender.close();sender.close();try{await sender.send(9);}catch(error){console.log(error.code,error.value);}queue.close();}

AsyncSender.name: share

examples.source: import {Channel} from 'std:futures';async function main():Task<void>{const queue=new Channel<int>(1);const first=queue.sender();const second=first.share();first.close();unwrap(second.trySend(42));console.log(await queue.receive());const closed=first.share();match(closed.trySend(7)){Err(error)=>console.log(error.code,error.value),Ok(_)=>{}}queue.close();}

parameters.label: callback: Owned<Function<T>> | Owned<Function<T, [TaskContext]>>
parameters.documentation: Starts one OS thread immediately and registers fallback joining with the returned owner. The callback runs once with zero arguments or one TaskContext; T is its return type and E its inferred thrown payload, or undefined. Returns Ok with a scoped handle or Err with code spawn and an OS message. Failed creation disposes the callback. No options or defaults. Leaving the owning scope waits for an unsettled worker, including on return or error. Moving the handle transfers cleanup responsibility. Fallback cleanup discards completion values and failures; use join to observe them. Cleanup never replaces a pending caller error, and can wait indefinitely for a worker that never finishes.

std:threads.name: spawn
std:threads.signature: spawn(callback: Owned<Function<T>> | Owned<Function<T, [TaskContext]>>): Result<Thread<T, E>, SpawnError>
std:threads.inferredSignature: function spawn(callback: Owned<Function<T>> | Owned<Function<T, [TaskContext]>>): Result<Thread<T, E>, SpawnError>

parameters.label: callback: Owned<Function<T>> | Owned<Function<T, [TaskContext]>>
parameters.documentation: Starts one native OS thread immediately. The callback runs once with zero arguments or one TaskContext. T is its returned type; E is its inferred thrown payload type, or undefined when it cannot throw. Returns Ok with a uniquely owned handle, or Err with code spawn and an OS error message. A failed spawn disposes the callback and its captures. Worker throws are retained for join; they do not throw in the spawning caller. No pool, serialization, cancellation or stack-size option is provided. Captures, returned values and thrown payloads must be owned transferable data. Caller loans, program-state borrows and stored callbacks are rejected.

std:threads.name: join
std:threads.signature: join(worker: Thread<T, E> | ScopedThread<T, E>): Result<T, ThreadError<E>>
std:threads.inferredSignature: function join(worker: Thread<T, E> | ScopedThread<T, E>): Result<T, ThreadError<E>>

parameters.label: worker: Thread<T, E> | ScopedThread<T, E>
parameters.documentation: Waits for the worker to finish and returns its owned result. Returns Err with code worker and the original typed error payload when the callback throws; code panic has no error payload and reports a backend panic. The handle is consumed on success and failure. The caller blocks until completion; there is no timeout or forced cancellation.

std:threads.name: detach
std:threads.signature: detach(worker: Thread<T, E> | ScopedThread<T, E>): void
std:threads.inferredSignature: function detach(worker: Thread<T, E> | ScopedThread<T, E>): void

parameters.label: worker: Thread<T, E> | ScopedThread<T, E>
parameters.documentation: Explicitly releases the caller’s handle without waiting. The worker continues independently; its eventual result and any error it throws are discarded. A runtime error such as integer overflow or an out-of-bounds index is a defect, so it is still printed to standard error as an uncaught error, without changing the exit code. Process exit does not wait for detached workers. Takes one handle and returns no value.

workers.documentation: Configured reusable worker count; nested helping can make running tasks exceed this count. Snapshot int; reading does not change the pool and later activity can change future snapshots. Dedicated threads are excluded. After const pool = new ThreadPool({workers:2,capacity:16}) and before submission, pool.stats().workers is 2. Ownership: copies the integer.

capacity.documentation: Configured maximum outstanding tasks, including completed results still retained. Snapshot int; reading does not change the pool and later activity can change future snapshots. Dedicated threads are excluded. After const pool = new ThreadPool({workers:2,capacity:16}) and before submission, pool.stats().capacity is 16. Ownership: copies the integer.

queued.documentation: Admitted tasks not yet started, including cancelled tasks awaiting disposal. Snapshot int; reading does not change the pool and later activity can change future snapshots. Dedicated threads are excluded. After const pool = new ThreadPool({workers:2,capacity:16}) and before submission, pool.stats().queued is 0. Ownership: copies the integer.

running.documentation: Started tasks not yet completed, including parents helping nested tasks. Snapshot int; reading does not change the pool and later activity can change future snapshots. Dedicated threads are excluded. After const pool = new ThreadPool({workers:2,capacity:16}) and before submission, pool.stats().running is 0. Ownership: copies the integer.

completed.documentation: Published task results still waiting for collection; joining or cleanup releases their slots. Snapshot int; reading does not change the pool and later activity can change future snapshots. Dedicated threads are excluded. After const pool = new ThreadPool({workers:2,capacity:16}) and before submission, pool.stats().completed is 0. Ownership: copies the integer.

outstanding.documentation: Total admitted tasks whose slots remain retained; equals queued + running + completed. Snapshot int; reading does not change the pool and later activity can change future snapshots. Dedicated threads are excluded. After const pool = new ThreadPool({workers:2,capacity:16}) and before submission, pool.stats().outstanding is 0. Ownership: copies the integer.

string.name: isWellFormed
string.documentation:
Tests whether text contains a valid Unicode representation. Takes no arguments; every native UTF-8 string returns true.

```tsrust
console.log("é😊".isWellFormed()); // prints "true"
```

Lone surrogate strings cannot be constructed in Tsrust. Receiver is borrowed and unchanged.

string.name: toWellFormed
string.documentation:
Returns unchanged string content. Takes no arguments and leaves the receiver reusable.

```tsrust
console.log("Hello".toWellFormed()); // prints "Hello"
```

Native strings are always valid UTF-8 and cannot contain lone surrogates. No surrogate replacement is needed. Static text can remain borrowed; owned text receives an independent copy.

string.name: trim
string.documentation:
Removes whitespace from both ends, preserving interior whitespace and returning a string without changing the receiver. Takes no arguments.

```tsrust
console.log("  Hello  ".trim()); // prints "Hello"
```

Whitespace includes Unicode whitespace: U+0085 is removed, while U+FEFF is preserved. Static text can retain a borrowed slice; owned input produces an independent copy.

string.name: trimStart
string.documentation:
Removes whitespace from the beginning, preserving interior whitespace and returning a string without changing the receiver. Takes no arguments.

```tsrust
console.log("  Hello  ".trimStart()); // prints "Hello  "
```

Whitespace includes Unicode whitespace: U+0085 is removed, while U+FEFF is preserved. Static text can retain a borrowed slice; owned input produces an independent copy.

string.name: trimEnd
string.documentation:
Removes whitespace from the end, preserving interior whitespace and returning a string without changing the receiver. Takes no arguments.

```tsrust
console.log("  Hello  ".trimEnd()); // prints "  Hello"
```

Whitespace includes Unicode whitespace: U+0085 is removed, while U+FEFF is preserved. Static text can retain a borrowed slice; owned input produces an independent copy.

string.name: trimLeft
string.documentation:
Removes whitespace from the beginning, preserving interior whitespace and returning a string without changing the receiver. Takes no arguments.

```tsrust
console.log("  Hello  ".trimLeft()); // prints "Hello  "
```

Whitespace includes Unicode whitespace: U+0085 is removed, while U+FEFF is preserved. Static text can retain a borrowed slice; owned input produces an independent copy. Alias of trimStart().

string.name: toLowerCase
string.documentation:
Converts text to lowercase using Unicode case mappings. Takes no arguments and leaves the original unchanged.

```tsrust
console.log("ÉCOLE".toLowerCase()); // prints "école"
```

Locale-independent conversion may expand characters and change byte length. The receiver is borrowed; the result owns its text.

string.name: toUpperCase
string.documentation:
Converts text to uppercase using Unicode case mappings. Takes no arguments and leaves the original unchanged.

```tsrust
console.log("Straße".toUpperCase()); // prints "STRASSE"
```

Locale-independent conversion may expand characters and change byte length. The receiver is borrowed; the result owns its text.

string.name: toLocaleLowerCase
string.documentation:
Returns the string converted to lowercase. The result is the same as `toLowerCase()`.

Takes no arguments. A locale argument such as `"tr"` is an `unsupported` error, because locale-specific rules are not provided; the conversion always uses the general Unicode mapping, whatever the system language is.

@returns A new string. A character can change length: `"İ"` becomes `i` followed by a combining dot.

```tsrust
console.log("ÉCOLE Straße".toLocaleLowerCase()); // prints "école straße"
```

Text in Turkish, Azerbaijani or Lithuanian can need rules that this conversion does not apply, for example dotted and dotless i.

The receiver is only read. The result is a new owned string.

string.name: toLocaleUpperCase
string.documentation:
Returns the string converted to uppercase. The result is the same as `toUpperCase()`.

Takes no arguments. A locale argument such as `"tr"` is an `unsupported` error, because locale-specific rules are not provided; the conversion always uses the general Unicode mapping, whatever the system language is.

@returns A new string. A character can change length: `"ß"` becomes `"SS"`.

```tsrust
console.log("école straße".toLocaleUpperCase()); // prints "ÉCOLE STRASSE"
```

Text in Turkish, Azerbaijani or Lithuanian can need rules that this conversion does not apply, for example dotted and dotless i.

The receiver is only read. The result is a new owned string.

string.name: includes
string.signature: includes(search: string | StringView | JsonValue | JsonView, position?: int): boolean
string.documentation:
Returns `true` when `search` occurs in the string. The string is unchanged.

@param search - Text to find, matched literally (no regular expressions or Unicode normalization).
@param position - Byte offset to start searching from, clamped to the string; defaults to zero.

```tsrust
console.log("hello".includes("ell")); // prints "true"
```

Positions are UTF-8 byte offsets, not UTF-16 units, and must fall on character boundaries. Also works on a `StringView`, and on a `JsonValue` or `JsonView` that a `typeof` check has shown holds a string, without copying the text.

Ownership: borrows the string and the search text.

string.name: startsWith
string.signature: startsWith(search: string | StringView | JsonValue | JsonView, position?: int): boolean
string.documentation:
Returns `true` when the string begins with `search` (at `position`, if given). The string is unchanged.

@param search - Text to find, matched literally (no regular expressions or Unicode normalization).
@param position - Byte offset to test at, clamped to the string; defaults to zero.

```tsrust
console.log("hello".startsWith("he")); // prints "true"
```

Positions are UTF-8 byte offsets, not UTF-16 units, and must fall on character boundaries. Also works on a `StringView`, and on a `JsonValue` or `JsonView` that a `typeof` check has shown holds a string, without copying the text.

Ownership: borrows the string and the search text.

@param search - Text to find, matched literally (no regular expressions or Unicode normalization).
@param position - Byte offset treated as the end, clamped to the string; defaults to byte length.

```tsrust
console.log("hello".endsWith("lo")); // prints "true"
```

Positions are UTF-8 byte offsets, not UTF-16 units, and must fall on character boundaries. Also works on a `StringView`, and on a `JsonValue` or `JsonView` that a `typeof` check has shown holds a string, without copying the text.

Ownership: borrows the string and the search text.

string.name: indexOf
string.signature: indexOf(search: string | StringView | JsonValue | JsonView, fromIndex?: int): int
string.documentation:
Returns the byte offset of the first occurrence of `search`, or -1 when absent. The string is unchanged.

@param search - Text to find, matched literally (no regular expressions or Unicode normalization).
@param fromIndex - Byte offset to start from; negative values clamp to zero, large values to byte length. Defaults to zero.

```tsrust
console.log("éclair".indexOf("c")); // prints "2"
```

Positions are UTF-8 byte offsets, not UTF-16 units, and must fall on character boundaries. Also works on a `StringView`, and on a `JsonValue` or `JsonView` that a `typeof` check has shown holds a string, without copying the text.

Ownership: borrows the string and the search text.

string.name: lastIndexOf
string.signature: lastIndexOf(search: string | StringView | JsonValue | JsonView, fromIndex?: int): int
string.documentation:
Returns the byte offset of the last occurrence of `search`, or -1 when absent. The string is unchanged.

@param search - Text to find, matched literally (no regular expressions or Unicode normalization).
@param fromIndex - Byte offset where the backward search starts; negative values clamp to zero, large values to byte length. Defaults to the end.

```tsrust
console.log("banana".lastIndexOf("a")); // prints "5"
```

Positions are UTF-8 byte offsets, not UTF-16 units, and must fall on character boundaries. Also works on a `StringView`, and on a `JsonValue` or `JsonView` that a `typeof` check has shown holds a string, without copying the text.

Ownership: borrows the string and the search text.

string.name: slice
string.documentation:
Returns the portion between start (inclusive) and end (exclusive). Both are optional integer byte offsets; defaults are zero and byte length. Negative offsets count from the end; bounds clamp to the string. Reversed bounds return empty text.

@param start - UTF-8 byte start offset. Negative values count from the end; bounds clamp. Defaults to zero.
@param end - Exclusive UTF-8 byte bound, default byte length. Negative values count from the end and bounds clamp.

```tsrust
console.log("hello".slice(1, 4)); // prints "ell"
```

Nonempty endpoints must be UTF-8 scalar boundaries. An offset inside a multi-byte character stops the program with a UTF-8 boundary error; `try`/`catch` cannot catch it, so derive offsets from `indexOf` or `length`. The receiver is borrowed; static slices may stay borrowed, owned slices copy.

string.name: substring
string.documentation:
Returns text between two clamped byte offsets. start is required; end defaults to byte length. Negative offsets clamp to zero and reversed bounds swap.

@param start - UTF-8 byte start offset. Required; negative bounds clamp to zero. Required.
@param end - Exclusive UTF-8 byte bound, default byte length. Reversed bounds swap; negative bounds clamp to zero.

```tsrust
console.log("hello".substring(4, 1)); // prints "ell"
```

Nonempty endpoints must be UTF-8 scalar boundaries; empty ranges skip boundary checks. An offset inside a multi-byte character stops the program with a UTF-8 boundary error; `try`/`catch` cannot catch it, so derive offsets from `indexOf` or `length`. Static slices can stay borrowed; owned results copy.

string.name: substr
string.documentation:
Returns up to `length` bytes starting at `start`, without changing the receiver. `start` and `length` accept any int, down to -9223372036854775808.

@param start - Byte offset; defaults to zero. Negative values count from the end; clamped to the string.
@param length - Byte count; length defaults to the remaining bytes. Values <= 0 give empty text, so a length <= 0 returns ""; larger values stop at the end.

```tsrust
console.log("hello".substr(1, 3)); // prints "ell"
console.log("hello".substr(-3, 2)); // prints "ll"
console.log("é😀x".substr(2, 4)); // prints "😀"
console.log("é".substr(1, 0)); // prints empty text
```

Unlike JavaScript, positions count UTF-8 bytes, not UTF-16 code units. Both ends of a nonempty result must fall on character boundaries: an end inside a multi-byte character stops the program (`try`/`catch` cannot catch it), so `"é".substr(1, 1)` fails. Any signed 64-bit int is accepted for either bound.

Ownership: borrows the string and returns a new string.

examples.source: const text = "hello".repeat(1); const piece = text.substr(1, 3); console.log(piece); console.log(text);

string.name: charAt
string.documentation:
Returns the Unicode scalar at an integer index, default zero. Negative or out-of-range indices return empty text.

@param index - Unicode scalar index, default zero; outside the string returns empty text.

```tsrust
console.log("é😊".charAt(1)); // prints "😊"
```

Counts Unicode scalars, unlike byte-indexed slice and JavaScript UTF-16 charAt. Receiver is borrowed; a selected scalar produces owned text.

string.name: concat
string.documentation:
Appends zero or more string arguments in order and returns the combined text. No coercion is performed; the receiver is unchanged.

@param values - Strings appended in order, without coercion.

```tsrust
console.log("Hello".concat(" ", "world")); // prints "Hello world"
```

Operands are borrowed. The result is independent of the receiver; static text may share immutable storage.

Spread arguments may come from strings, arrays or Sets whose elements are strings. String sources construct Unicode scalar character values and stay usable.

```tsrust
console.log("a".concat(..."bc"));
// prints abc
```

string.name: padStart
string.documentation:
Pads the beginning until the integer target byte length is reached. Optional filler defaults to a space and repeats as needed. Short/negative targets or empty filler leave text unchanged.

@param target - Destination byte length of the padded string; short or negative targets leave it unchanged.
@param filler - String repeated to fill missing bytes; defaults to one space, empty text disables padding.

```tsrust
console.log("7".padStart(3, "0")); // prints "007"
```

Targets count UTF-8 bytes, not JavaScript UTF-16 units. A truncated filler must end at a scalar boundary or fail. A filler cut inside a multi-byte character stops the program with a UTF-8 boundary error; `try`/`catch` cannot catch it. Receiver stays reusable; changed results own their storage, no-ops use Cow cloning.

string.name: padEnd
string.documentation:
Pads the end until the integer target byte length is reached. Optional filler defaults to a space and repeats as needed. Short/negative targets or empty filler leave text unchanged.

@param target - Destination byte length of the padded string; short or negative targets leave it unchanged.
@param filler - String repeated to fill missing bytes; defaults to one space, empty text disables padding.

```tsrust
console.log("7".padEnd(3, "0")); // prints "700"
```

Targets count UTF-8 bytes, not JavaScript UTF-16 units. A truncated filler must end at a scalar boundary or fail. A filler cut inside a multi-byte character stops the program with a UTF-8 boundary error; `try`/`catch` cannot catch it. Receiver stays reusable; changed results own their storage, no-ops use Cow cloning.

string.name: repeat
string.documentation:
Repeats the receiver count times, returning new text. count is a required nonnegative integer; zero produces empty text. Negative counts and excessive lengths fail.

@param count - Nonnegative integer repetition count; zero returns empty text.

```tsrust
console.log("ha".repeat(3)); // prints "hahaha"
```

Receiver is borrowed; output has independent storage.

string.name: replace
string.documentation:
Replaces the first occurrence of string search with replacement text. The original remains unchanged. Regular expressions are unsupported.

@param search - Text to find; matched literally, without regular expressions or Unicode normalization.
@param replacement - Replacement text; supports $$, $&, $` and $' templates.

```tsrust
console.log("banana".replace("a", "o")); // prints "bonana"
```

Replacement templates support $$ (literal dollar), $& (match), $` (prefix) and $' (suffix); capture references have no regex groups. Operands are borrowed; output owns its text.

string.name: replaceAll
string.documentation:
Replaces every non-overlapping occurrence of string search with replacement text. The original remains unchanged. Regular expressions are unsupported.

@param search - Text to find; matched literally, without regular expressions or Unicode normalization.
@param replacement - Replacement text; supports $$, $&, $` and $' templates.

```tsrust
console.log("banana".replaceAll("a", "o")); // prints "bonono"
```

Replacement templates support $$ (literal dollar), $& (match), $` (prefix) and $' (suffix); capture references have no regex groups. Operands are borrowed; output owns its text.

string.name: split
string.documentation:
Splits the string at each `separator` and returns the pieces. The string is unchanged.

@param separator - Literal text to split at. Omission returns the whole string as one element. Empty text splits into single characters (Unicode scalars, not UTF-16 units).
@param limit - Maximum number of pieces, as in JavaScript: converted modulo 2^32, defaults to 4294967295 (-1 means the same; 4294967296 converts to zero, which returns an empty array). Pieces beyond the limit are discarded.

```tsrust
const parts = "a,b,c".split(",", 2);
console.log(parts.length); // prints "2"
console.log(parts[1]); // prints "b", not "b,c"
console.log("😀é".split("").length); // prints "2"
console.log("".split("").length); // prints "0"
console.log("".split().length); // prints "1"
console.log("a,b".split(",", -1).length); // prints "2"
console.log("a,b".split(",", 4294967296).length); // prints "0"
```

Separators match literally and do not overlap. Leading, adjacent and trailing separators produce empty pieces: `"a,,".split(",")` has three elements. Regular expressions are not supported.

Ownership: borrows the string; the returned array is independent.

examples.source: const parts = "😀é".split(""); console.log(parts.length); console.log(parts[0]); console.log(parts[1]); console.log("e\u0301".split("").length);

console.log("".split("").length); console.log("".split().length); console.log("a,b".split(",", -1).length); console.log("a,b".split(",", 0).length); console.log("a,b".split(",", 4294967296).length); console.log("a,b".split(",", 4294967297).length);
const text = "a,b".repeat(1); const parts = text.split(); console.log(parts[0]); console.log(text);

string.documentation:
Returns the number of bytes in the UTF-8 representation. This read-only property does not change the receiver.

```tsrust
console.log("é😊".length); // prints "6"
```

A StringView supports this read directly. A JsonValue or JsonView proven to contain a string by a stable typeof guard also supports this read without copying or consuming its text. The source owner stays borrowed for the complete operation; later arguments cannot invalidate it.

string.name: valueOf
string.documentation:

```tsrust
console.log("Hello".valueOf()); // prints "Hello"
```

string.documentation:

string.name: at
string.documentation:
Returns the character at a position counted from the start, or from the end when the position is negative.

@param index - Required int position. `0` is the first character and `-1` is the last. Positions count whole Unicode characters, so an accented letter or an emoji is one position.

Returns the character as a one-character string, or `undefined` when the position is outside the string. The result type is `string | undefined`; use `??` for a fallback or compare with `undefined` before using it as a string.

```tsrust
const text = "aé😀b";
console.log(String(text.at(0)), String(text.at(-1)), String(text.at(2))); // prints "a b 😀"
```

```tsrust
const text = "ab";
console.log(String(text.at(2)), text.at(5) ?? "none"); // prints "undefined none"
```

Calling it with no argument or more than one is an `arity` error; a number or string index is a `type` error. Unlike `charAt`, which returns an empty string for a missing position, `at` returns `undefined` and accepts negative positions.

Positions count Unicode characters, not UTF-16 code units: `"😀".at(0)` is the whole emoji.

Receiver is borrowed and unchanged; the returned character is a new string owned by the caller.

const code = "A".codePointAt();
if (code !== undefined) { console.log(code + 1, String.fromCodePoint(code + 1)); }

string.name: normalize
string.documentation:
Returns the text in a Unicode normal form, so different spellings of the same characters (such as `é` as one character or as `e` plus an accent) become identical.

@param form - `"NFC"` (default), `"NFD"`, `"NFKC"` or `"NFKD"`, case-sensitive. NFC composes characters; NFD decomposes them. NFKC and NFKD also replace compatibility characters, such as ligatures and circled digits, with ordinary ones.

It does not change case, strip accents or apply language rules. The length can change.

```tsrust
const text = "é";
console.log(text.normalize(), "é".normalize("NFD")); // prints é é
```

```tsrust
console.log("ﬁ①가".normalize("NFKC"), "가".normalize("NFD")); // prints fi1가 가
```

Any other form name, including lowercase `"nfc"` or `""`, stops the program with `normalize form must be NFC, NFD, NFKC or NFKD` and the call's source position.

Ownership: the receiver and form are borrowed; the result is a new string.

Array.name: toString
Array.documentation:
Returns the array element text joined with commas, the same as `join()`. The array is unchanged. Takes no arguments; passing any, including undefined, is an error. An empty array gives an empty string. The result is UTF-8 text.

Nested arrays add their own comma-separated text, `null` and `undefined` add empty text, records add `[object Object]`. Numbers print as in JavaScript: negative zero becomes 0, and `NaN`, `Infinity`, `-Infinity` print as such; digits can differ at rounding boundaries. Ints keep their full signed 64-bit value.

```tsrust
const values: int[][] = [[1, 2], [], [3]];
console.log(values.toString()); // prints "1,2,,3"
```

```tsrust
const values: null[] = [null, null];
console.log(values.toString()); // prints ","
```

Arrays of `void` cannot be converted to text.

Ownership: evaluated once and borrowed; returns an independently owned string.

Array.name: join
Array.documentation:
Returns the elements as one string with `separator` between them. The array is unchanged. Lengths and text are UTF-8.

@param separator - Text placed between elements; defaults to a comma. Must be a string. More than one argument, or explicit undefined, is an error.

Nested arrays use commas inside, whatever the separator. `null` and `undefined` add empty text, records add `[object Object]`, and numbers print as in JavaScript (negative zero becomes 0; ints keep their full signed 64-bit value). An empty array returns an empty string.

```tsrust
const values: int[][] = [[1, 2], [], [3]];
console.log(values.join("|")); // prints "1,2||3"
```

```tsrust
const values: null[] = [null, null];
console.log(values.join("|")); // prints "|"
```

Arrays of `void` cannot be converted to text.

Ownership: evaluates the array and separator once, left to right, borrows both, and returns an independently owned string.

Array.name: values
toLocaleString
Array.documentation:
Returns the elements as text separated by commas, with numbers formatted for display. Takes no arguments; the array is unchanged. Nested arrays are flattened into the text.

Numbers get comma thousands separators, a period decimal point and at most three decimals (ties round away from zero; `-0` stays `-0`; infinities show as `∞`). Ints keep their full signed 64-bit range. These rules do not depend on the system language. Strings, booleans and `[object Object]` for records print as in `join()`; `null` and `undefined` add empty text.

```tsrust
const values: number[] = [1000.5, -0.0, 1.2345];
console.log(values.toLocaleString()); // prints 1,000.5,-0,1.235
```

```tsrust
const values: int[][] = [[1000], [], [2000, 3000]];
console.log(values.toLocaleString(), [null, null].toLocaleString()); // prints 1,000,,2,000,3,000 ,
```

The result is display text: commas inside elements are not escaped. Locale and options arguments are not supported, nor is `void[]`.

Ownership: borrows the array and returns a new string.

Number.name: parseFloat
Number.documentation:
Parses the longest decimal prefix after leading ECMAScript whitespace. Accepts one string, optional sign, decimal fraction/exponent or Infinity. Incomplete exponents stop before the exponent; invalid starts return NaN.

@param text - Borrowed string to parse; a valid decimal/Infinity prefix is accepted despite trailing text.

```tsrust
console.log(Number.parseFloat("  1.25tail")); // prints "1.25"
```

Unlike Number(text), trailing text is permitted. Results use 64-bit floating-point precision; overflow produces Infinity, underflow can produce zero, and signed zero is preserved. Input is borrowed without a parsing buffer.

Number.name: parseInt
Number.documentation:
Reads a whole number from the start of a string and returns it as a number. Leading spaces are skipped, an optional `+` or `-` sign is accepted, and reading stops at the first character that is not a digit of the radix, so trailing text is ignored.

@param text - String to read. It is not changed.
@param radix - Optional int base from 2 through 36; letters `a` to `z` (either case) are digits above 9. When omitted or `0`, base 10 is used, or base 16 when the digits start with `0x` or `0X`. With radix 16 a `0x` prefix is also accepted.

Returns `NaN` when no digit can be read, for example an empty string, `"abc"` or `"0x"`, and when the radix is outside 2 through 36. A fraction is not read: `"3.9"` gives `3`.

```tsrust
console.log(Number.parseInt("42px"), Number.parseInt("  -17"), Number.parseInt("3.9")); // prints "42 -17 3"
```

```tsrust
console.log(Number.parseInt("ff", 16), Number.parseInt("0x1F"), Number.parseInt("101", 2)); // prints "255 31 5"
```

```tsrust
console.log(Number.parseInt("abc"), Number.parseInt("12", 1), Number.isNaN(Number.parseInt(""))); // prints "NaN NaN true"
```

Calling it with no argument or more than two is an `arity` error. The first argument must be a string and the radix an int; a number radix such as `10.5` is a `type` error. The result is a `number`, not an `int`, because it can be `NaN`; assigning it to an `int` is a `type` error. Values beyond 9007199254740992 are rounded to the nearest representable number.

The string is borrowed for the call and stays usable; the result is a plain number.

Math.name: f16round
Math.documentation:
Rounds a number to the nearest value that 16-bit (half precision) floating point can hold, and returns it as a number.

@param value - Required number. An int needs `Number(...)` first; other types are a `type` error. A missing or extra argument is an `arity` error.

@returns The nearest half-precision value. A value exactly halfway between two candidates goes to the one with an even last bit. Magnitudes of 65520 and above give `Infinity` with the sign of the input. Magnitudes too small for half precision give zero with the sign of the input. `NaN`, infinities and zeros are returned unchanged.

```tsrust
console.log(Math.f16round(1.337), Math.f16round(2049.0), Math.f16round(65520.0)); // prints "1.3369140625 2048 Infinity"
```

Half precision keeps about three significant decimal digits, so most inputs change. Use `Math.fround` for single precision.

The argument is copied; nothing is allocated.

Math.name: random
Math.documentation:
Returns a pseudo-random number that is at least 0 and less than 1. Every value in that range is about equally likely.

Takes no arguments; passing one is an `arity` error.

@returns A `number` from 0 (possible) up to but not including 1. The result is never an `int`.

```tsrust
const roll = Math.floor(Math.random() * 6.0) + 1.0;
console.log(roll >= 1.0 && roll <= 6.0, Math.random() < 1.0); // prints "true true"
```

Scale and shift the result for other ranges: `low + Math.random() * (high - low)`. Each run of a program produces a different sequence, and the sequence cannot be seeded. Each thread has its own sequence.

Do not use the result for passwords, tokens or anything else that must be unpredictable.

Nothing is borrowed or allocated.

examples.source:
const roll = Math.floor(Math.random() * 6.0) + 1.0;
console.log(roll >= 1.0 && roll <= 6.0, Math.random() < 1.0);

@param b - Second number, converted to signed 32-bit multiplication bits.

```tsrust
console.log(Math.imul(3.0, 4.0)); // prints "12"
```

Uses standard native f64 arithmetic. Transcendental results may differ slightly across platforms. Primitive arguments are copied; no owned result storage is allocated.

console.name: log
console.documentation:
Prints values to stdout, separated by spaces, followed by a newline. No arguments prints a blank line. Top-level strings print without quotes; arrays and records are shown with quoted strings, nested 2 levels deep and up to 100 array elements.

@param values - Values to print. If the first value is a string and more follow, it is a format string: `%s` text, `%d` number, `%i` integer, `%f` float, `%j` JSON, `%o` detailed inspection, `%O` default inspection, `%c` style (ignored), `%%` a literal %. Extra values are appended with spaces.

```tsrust
console.log("user: %s, age: %d", "Pat", 7); // stdout: user: Pat, age: 7
```

Nullable values print their present payload, `null`, or `undefined`. Functions, mixed-type arrays and cyclic objects cannot be printed.

Ownership: borrows the values.

Omitted condition is false-like; false, zero, NaN and empty text are false-like, while arrays and records are true-like.

@param values - Optional message using the same placeholders as log.

boolean.name: valueOf
boolean.documentation:
Returns the same primitive value without conversion or boxing. Takes no arguments; the receiver is unchanged.

```tsrust
const value: boolean = true;
console.log(value.valueOf()); // prints "true"
```

Primitive values are copied without allocation.

boolean.documentation:
Returns "true" or "false" according to the receiver. Takes no arguments; the original boolean is unchanged.

```tsrust
const value: boolean = false;

```

Returns static borrowed text without allocating.

number.name: valueOf
number.documentation:
Returns the same primitive value without conversion or boxing. Takes no arguments; the receiver is unchanged.

```tsrust
const value: number = 1.5;
console.log(value.valueOf()); // prints "1.5"
```

Primitive values are copied without allocation.

number.name: toFixed
number.documentation:
Returns decimal text with fractionDigits places after the decimal point. Rounds halfway values to the nearest even digit (half to even). 0 through 100; omission means zero decimal places. Exact negative zero formats as positive zero. Special values use NaN and Infinity. JavaScript halfway rounding may differ.

@param fractionDigits - Integer number of digits after the decimal point, from 0 through 100; defaults to zero.

```tsrust
const value: number = 1.25;
console.log(value.toFixed(2)); // prints "1.25"
```

Receiver remains unchanged; result owns UTF-8 text. Precision must be int; invalid runtime bounds fail.

number.name: toExponential
number.documentation:
Returns scientific notation with fractionDigits places after the decimal point and a signed exponent. Rounds halfway values to the nearest even digit (half to even). 0 through 100; omission uses shortest scientific digits. Exact negative zero formats as positive zero. Special values use NaN and Infinity. JavaScript halfway rounding may differ.

@param fractionDigits - Integer number of digits after the decimal point, from 0 through 100; defaults to shortest scientific digits.

```tsrust
const value: number = 1.25;
console.log(value.toExponential(2)); // prints "1.25e+0"
```

Receiver remains unchanged; result owns UTF-8 text. Precision must be int; invalid runtime bounds fail.

number.name: toPrecision
number.documentation:
Returns text with precision significant digits, choosing decimal or scientific notation according to magnitude. Rounds halfway values to the nearest even digit (half to even). 1 through 100; omission uses shortest decimal digits. Exact negative zero formats as positive zero. Special values use NaN and Infinity. JavaScript halfway rounding may differ.

@param precision - Integer significant-digit count from 1 through 100; omission uses shortest decimal formatting.

```tsrust
const value: number = 1.25;
console.log(value.toPrecision(3)); // prints "1.25"
```

Receiver remains unchanged; result owns UTF-8 text. Precision must be int; invalid runtime bounds fail.

number.name: toString
number.documentation:
Returns the number as text. With no argument the text is the shortest decimal form that reads back as the same number. With a radix the number is written in that base.

@param radix - Optional int base from 2 through 36; digits above 9 are the lowercase letters `a` to `z`. Defaults to 10.

In another base, a fraction is written after a `.` using as many digits as are needed to read back the same number, so `0.1` in base 2 is a long repeating pattern. A negative number starts with `-`. `NaN`, `Infinity` and `-Infinity` print as those words in every base, and negative zero prints as `0`. Very large or very small numbers use exponent form only in base 10, for example `1e+21`.

```tsrust
const value = 255.5;
console.log(value.toString(), value.toString(16), value.toString(2)); // prints "255.5 ff.8 11111111.1"
```

```tsrust
const third = 1.0 / 3.0;
console.log(third.toString(3), (0.1).toString(8), (-7.25).toString(2)); // prints "0.1 0.0631463146314631464 -111.01"
```

```tsrust
const big = 1e21;
console.log(big.toString(), big.toString(36), (0.0 / 0.0).toString(2)); // prints "1e+21 5v1j4f4ds7c000 NaN"
```

More than one argument is an `arity` error and a radix that is not an int is a `type` error. A radix outside 2 through 36 stops the program with `number.toString radix must be between 2 and 36` and the source position. Above 9007199254740992 a number cannot hold every whole value, so low digits it cannot represent print as `0`.

The receiver is copied; the result is a new string owned by the caller.

int.name: toString
int.documentation:
Formats a signed native i64 as lowercase digits. Optional radix is an int from 2 through 36, default 10. Negatives retain a leading minus in every radix; invalid radices fail.

@param radix - Integer base from 2 through 36, default 10; invalid bases fail.

```tsrust
const value: int = -255;
console.log(value.toString(16)); // prints "-ff"
```

Supports the complete i64 range, unlike JavaScript Number’s safe-integer range. Receiver is copied; result owns independent UTF-8 text.

globals.name: Number
globals.signature: Number(value?: int | number | boolean | string | null | undefined): number
parameters: value?: int | number | boolean | string | null | undefined
globals.documentation:
Converts a value to a number: no argument or `null` gives 0, `undefined` gives `NaN`, `true`/`false` give 1/0. Strings are trimmed and parsed as a whole decimal, `Infinity`, or a `0b`/`0o`/`0x` integer; empty text gives 0 and invalid text `NaN`. Signed zero is preserved. Text may be decimal, signed Infinity or an unsigned 0b/0o/0x integer. Whitespace trimming includes U+0085.

@param value - Optional primitive: int, number, boolean, string, null, undefined or a union of these. Arrays, records and functions are type errors; enums convert their value.

```tsrust
const value: string | undefined = "12.5";
console.log(Number(value), Number(true), Number(null), Number.isNaN(Number(undefined))); // 12.5 1 0 true
```

A scalar union converts its active alternative. Large ints may round to the nearest number. Radix prefixes cannot have a sign; digit separators and trailing text make `NaN`. Unary `+` converts the same way (an int stays an int).

```tsrust
console.log(Number("0x10"), +"0b11", Number("0o17"), Number.isNaN(Number("12tail"))); // 16 3 15 true
```

Ownership: borrows the argument and returns a number.

undefined

globals.name: void
Boolean
globals.documentation:
Converts a value to `true` or `false`. `false`, `0`, `-0`, `NaN`, `""`, `null`, `undefined`, no argument and a `void` result are `false`; everything else is `true`, including empty arrays and records. A union converts its current alternative.

@param value - Optional value of any supported type; defaults to undefined.

```tsrust
console.log(Boolean(null), Boolean("false"), Boolean([])); // false true true
```

Conditions require a `boolean`; use this for an explicit conversion. `new Boolean` is not supported.

Ownership: borrows the argument and returns a boolean.

globals.name: String
globals.documentation:
Converts a value to text. No argument gives `""`; `null` gives `"null"`, `undefined` (or a `void` result) `"undefined"`. Numbers print as in JavaScript (`-0` becomes 0) and ints keep their signed 64-bit value. Arrays and tuples join their elements with commas, including all supported nested-array text; records give `[object Object]`. Functions cannot be converted, including whole nullable unions with a callable payload; narrow with a strict guard first. The argument is borrowed.

@param value - Optional primitive, array or record. Functions cannot be converted; narrow a union that may hold one first.

```tsrust
console.log(String(null), String(undefined), String([null, null]), String(-0.0)); // null undefined , 0
```

Custom `toString` and `valueOf` methods are not used.

Ownership: borrows the argument and returns an independently owned string.

globals.name: Array
globals.documentation:
Static array functions: `Array.isArray(value)` tests for an array, `Array.of(...items)` builds one from its arguments, and Array.from creates one (`Array.from(source, map?)`) from an array, string characters, `Set` values or `Map` entries, optionally mapping each. There is no `new Array(...)`.

Array literals also accept spreads: `[0, ...values, 1]` adds every element in order, evaluating each part left to right, and strings, Sets and Maps can be spread too.

```tsrust
console.log(Array.isArray([1]), Array.isArray(null)); // true false
```

Ownership: scalar elements are copied; owned elements move into the new array. `Array.isArray` only borrows its argument.

globals.name: Task

examples.source: async function answer(): Task<int> { return 42; } async function main(): Task<void> { const task = answer(); console.log(await task); }

globals.name: Function

examples.source:
const double: Function<int, [int]> = (value: int): int => { return value * 2; };
console.log(double(4));

const pick: Function<int, [first: int, second?: int, ...rest: int[]]> = (first: int, second?: int, ...rest: int[]): int => { return first + rest.length; };
console.log(pick(1), pick(1, 2, 3, 4));

ReadOnly
