const keep: ReadOnly<Function<string, [Owned<string>]>> = (text: string): string => { return text; };
console.log(keep("moved".repeat(1)));

globals.name: Object
globals.documentation:
Provides functions that work on any value. `Object.is` tests whether two values are the same value, treating `NaN` as itself and telling `0` from `-0`.

```tsrust
console.log(Object.is(1, 1), Object.is("a", "b")); // prints "true false"
```

Object is a namespace of functions here; it is not a constructor and cannot be called or used as a type.

globals.name: parseInt
globals.documentation:
Reads a whole number from the start of a string and returns it as a number. It is the same function as `Number.parseInt`. Leading spaces are skipped, an optional `+` or `-` sign is accepted, and reading stops at the first character that is not a digit of the radix, so trailing text is ignored.

@param text - String to read. It is not changed.
@param radix - Optional int base from 2 through 36; letters `a` to `z` (either case) are digits above 9. When omitted or `0`, base 10 is used, or base 16 when the digits start with `0x` or `0X`.

@returns A `number`. `NaN` when no digit can be read, for example an empty string or `"abc"`, and when the radix is outside 2 through 36. A fraction is not read: `"3.9"` gives `3`.

```tsrust
console.log(parseInt("42px"), parseInt("  -17"), parseInt("3.9")); // prints "42 -17 3"
```

```tsrust
console.log(parseInt("ff", 16), parseInt("0x1F"), parseInt("101", 2), parseInt("abc")); // prints "255 31 5 NaN"
```

Calling it with no argument or more than two is an `arity` error. The text must be a string and the radix an int, otherwise a `type` error. The result is a `number`, not an `int`, because it can be `NaN`; assigning it to an `int` is a `type` error. Passing `parseInt` itself as a value, as in `texts.map(parseInt)`, is unsupported; write `texts.map((text) => parseInt(text))`. A function or variable that you declare with the name `parseInt` takes precedence.

The string is borrowed for the call and stays usable; the result is a plain number.

globals.name: parseFloat
globals.documentation:
Reads a decimal number from the start of a string and returns it as a number. It is the same function as `Number.parseFloat`. Leading spaces are skipped. An optional sign, digits, a fraction, an exponent and the word `Infinity` are accepted, and reading stops at the first character that does not continue the number.

@param text - String to read. It is not changed.

@returns A `number`. `NaN` when the text does not start with a number, for example an empty string or `"abc"`.

```tsrust
console.log(parseFloat("1.25tail"), parseFloat("  -2e3"), parseFloat(".5"), parseFloat("abc")); // prints "1.25 -2000 0.5 NaN"
```

Exactly one string argument is required: another count is an `arity` error and another type a `type` error. A value too large for a number gives `Infinity`. Passing `parseFloat` itself as a value is unsupported; wrap it in an arrow function. A function or variable that you declare with the name `parseFloat` takes precedence.

The string is borrowed for the call and stays usable; the result is a plain number.

globals.name: isNaN

examples.source: const parsed = parseInt("abc"); console.log(isNaN(parsed), isNaN(1.5), isNaN(Infinity), parsed === NaN);

globals.name: isFinite
globals.documentation:
Tests whether a number is an ordinary finite value. It is the same function as `Number.isFinite`.

@param value - Number to test. An int is accepted and is always finite.

@returns `false` for `Infinity`, `-Infinity` and `NaN`; `true` for every other number.

```tsrust
console.log(isFinite(2.5), isFinite(1.0 / 0.0), isFinite(-Infinity), isFinite(NaN)); // prints "true false false false"
```

Exactly one number is required: another count is an `arity` error, and a string, boolean or other type is a `type` error because no value is converted to a number first; convert explicitly with `Number(value)`. A function or variable that you declare with the name `isFinite` takes precedence.

The number is copied; nothing is changed or allocated.

globals.name: NaN
globals.documentation:
The not-a-number value, the same value as `Number.NaN`. Arithmetic produces it for an undefined result such as `0.0 / 0.0`, and `parseInt` and `parseFloat` return it when text holds no number. It takes no arguments.

```tsrust
const missing = NaN;
console.log(missing, missing === NaN, isNaN(missing), missing + 1.0, typeof missing); // prints "NaN false true NaN number"
```

`NaN` is not equal to any value, itself included, so `value === NaN` is always `false`; test with `isNaN(value)`. Any arithmetic with `NaN` gives `NaN`, and every ordering comparison with it is `false`. Its type is `number`; assigning it to an `int` is a `type` error. It cannot be assigned to. A variable or parameter that you declare with the name `NaN` takes precedence.

The value is a plain copied number.

examples.source: const missing = NaN; console.log(missing, missing === NaN, isNaN(missing), missing + 1.0, typeof missing);

globals.name: Infinity

examples.source: let lowest = Infinity; for (const value of [4.5, 2.5, 8.0]) { if (value < lowest) { lowest = value; } } console.log(lowest, Infinity > Number.MAX_VALUE, -Infinity, isFinite(Infinity));

globals.name: Set
globals.signature: new Set<Element>(source?: Element[] | Set<Element> | string | null | undefined): Set<Element>
parameters: source?: Element[] | Set<Element> | string | null | undefined
globals.documentation:
Constructs an owned set of unique keys in insertion order. Without a source, use an explicit key type or a contextual Set type. Arrays and sets provide keys; strings provide Unicode characters and require string keys. Null and undefined create an empty set. Duplicate keys are omitted; negative number zero is stored as positive zero. Keys are int, number, boolean, string, null, undefined, enums, or unions of those values. Number keys use SameValueZero: NaN equals NaN and both zeros are the same key. Record, array, and function identity keys are unsupported.

```tsrust
const values = new Set<int>([2, 1, 2]);
console.log(values.size); // 2
```

Ownership: construction explicitly copies source keys; the source remains usable. Ordinary bindings and access never implicitly clone a set.

globals.name: Map
globals.signature: new Map<Key, Value>(source?: [Key, Value][] | Map<Key, Value> | null | undefined): Map<Key, Value>
parameters: source?: [Key, Value][] | Map<Key, Value> | null | undefined

examples.source: const values = new Map<string, int>(); values.set("a", 1); console.log(values.size);

globals.name: unwrap

parameters.label: result: Result<T, E>
parameters.documentation: Returns the Ok payload or throws the original Err payload through ordinary try/catch/finally. Takes one Result, with no defaults or additional options. Result<void, E> returns no value on success. Errors retain their type and owned contents; unwrap does not panic or stringify them. Use match when each failure needs local recovery.

examples.source: import {spawn,join} from 'std:threads';function main(){const first=unwrap(spawn(():int=>20));const second=unwrap(spawn(():int=>22));const a=unwrap(join(first));const b=unwrap(join(second));console.log(a+b);}

RuntimeError
globals.signature: type RuntimeError = { name: string; code: string; message: string; source: string; start: int; end: int; line: int; column: int }
globals.documentation:
The error value of a runtime fault, as received by `catch` and by the error side of a `Checked` result.

- `name`: the error class, such as `RangeError` for overflow and length limits or `TypeError` for a failed non-null assertion.
- `code`: a short stable identifier, such as `overflow`, `bounds` or `capacity`.
- `message`: the description, ending with `at source bytes A..B`.
- `source`: the path of the file that faulted.
- `start`, `end`: byte offsets of the failing expression in that file.
- `line`, `column`: its 1-based position (columns count UTF-16 code units).

```tsrust
function scale(value: int): Checked<int> {
  return value * 4611686018427387904;
}
// scale(2) fails with name 'RangeError', code 'overflow', line 2, column 16
```

A module that declares its own `RuntimeError` type uses that declaration instead.

Ownership: the record owns its strings; matching or catching it moves it to the handler.

Object.name: is
Object.documentation:
Tests whether two values are the same value. It is stricter about numbers than `===`: `NaN` is the same as `NaN`, and `0` is not the same as `-0`.

@param left - First value.
@param right - Second value.

An `int` and a `number` with the same value are the same. Strings compare by text. An array or record is the same only as itself: two separate arrays with equal contents are not the same. Values of different kinds are never the same. Unions compare their current alternatives; functions are not accepted (`unsupported`).

```tsrust
console.log(Object.is(Number.NaN, Number.NaN), Object.is(0.0, -0.0), Object.is(1, 1.0)); // prints "true false true"
```

```tsrust
const a = [1];
const b = [1];
console.log(Object.is(a, a), Object.is(a, b), Object.is("x", "x")); // prints "true false true"
```

```tsrust
console.log(Object.is(1, "1"), Object.is(null, undefined), Object.is(null, null)); // prints "false false true"
```

Both values are borrowed for the comparison and stay usable.

Set.name: size
Set.documentation:
Returns the number of distinct keys. Readonly; assigning this property is rejected.

Keys are int, number, boolean, string, null, undefined, enums, or unions of those values. Number keys use SameValueZero: NaN equals NaN and both zeros are the same key. Record, array, and function identity keys are unsupported.

```tsrust
const values = new Set<int>([2, 1, 2]);
console.log(values.size); // 2
```

Set.name: add
Set.documentation:
Inserts a key if absent. A duplicate leaves order unchanged. Returns void; chaining is unsupported. Deleting and adding a key again places it last. Ownership: owned keys transfer into the set; scalar keys copy.

Keys are int, number, boolean, string, null, undefined, enums, or unions of those values. Number keys use SameValueZero: NaN equals NaN and both zeros are the same key. Record, array, and function identity keys are unsupported.

```tsrust
const values = new Set<int>([2, 1, 2]);
values.add(3);
console.log(values.size); // 3
```

examples.source: const values = new Set<int>([2, 1, 2]); values.add(3); console.log(values.size);

Set.name: has
Set.documentation:
Reports whether a matching key exists. Receiver and argument are borrowed and unchanged.

Keys are int, number, boolean, string, null, undefined, enums, or unions of those values. Number keys use SameValueZero: NaN equals NaN and both zeros are the same key. Record, array, and function identity keys are unsupported.

```tsrust
const values = new Set<int>([2, 1, 2]);
console.log(values.has(2)); // true
```

Set.name: delete
Set.documentation:
Removes a matching key and returns true, or returns false if absent. Surviving keys keep their order. Argument is borrowed; receiver mutates.

Keys are int, number, boolean, string, null, undefined, enums, or unions of those values. Number keys use SameValueZero: NaN equals NaN and both zeros are the same key. Record, array, and function identity keys are unsupported.

```tsrust
const values = new Set<int>([2, 1, 2]);
console.log(values.delete(2), values.size); // true 1
```

examples.source: const values = new Set<int>([2, 1, 2]); console.log(values.delete(2), values.size);

Set.name: clear
Set.documentation:
Removes every key. Returns void. Receiver mutates.

Keys are int, number, boolean, string, null, undefined, enums, or unions of those values. Number keys use SameValueZero: NaN equals NaN and both zeros are the same key. Record, array, and function identity keys are unsupported.

```tsrust
const values = new Set<int>([2, 1, 2]);
values.clear();
console.log(values.size); // 0
```

examples.source: const values = new Set<int>([2, 1, 2]); values.clear(); console.log(values.size);

Set.name: values
Set.documentation:
Returns an independent array of keys in insertion order. Takes no arguments. This is an array snapshot, not a live iterator. Receiver is borrowed; keys are explicitly copied.

Keys are int, number, boolean, string, null, undefined, enums, or unions of those values. Number keys use SameValueZero: NaN equals NaN and both zeros are the same key. Record, array, and function identity keys are unsupported.

```tsrust
const values = new Set<int>([2, 1, 2]);
console.log(values.values().join(",")); // 2,1
```

Keys are int, number, boolean, string, null, undefined, enums, or unions of those values. Number keys use SameValueZero: NaN equals NaN and both zeros are the same key. Record, array, and function identity keys are unsupported.

```tsrust

console.log(values.keys().join(",")); // 2,1
```

Map.name: size
Map.documentation:
Returns the number of distinct keys. This property is readonly; assignment is rejected. It takes no arguments.

Keys must match the declared key type. Scalar, enum and union keys are supported; record, array and function identity keys are unsupported. Number keys use SameValueZero: NaN equals NaN, and both zeros are one key. Wrong argument counts or incompatible argument types are static errors.

```tsrust
const values = new Map<string, int>();
values.set("a", 1);
console.log(values.size); // 1
```

Ownership: receiver is read and unchanged.

examples.source: const values = new Map<string, int>(); values.set("a", 1); console.log(values.size);

Map.name: set

examples.source: const values = new Map<string, int>(); values.set("a", 1); values.set("a", 3); console.log(values.size, values.get("a") ?? 0);

Map.name: get
Map.documentation:
Reads the value for a key, or returns undefined when absent. Stored undefined remains distinguishable through has(). Receiver is unchanged.

Keys must match the declared key type. Scalar, enum and union keys are supported; record, array and function identity keys are unsupported. Number keys use SameValueZero: NaN equals NaN, and both zeros are one key. Wrong argument counts or incompatible argument types are static errors.

```tsrust
const values = new Map<string, int>();
values.set("a", 1);
console.log(values.get("a") ?? 0, values.get("missing") ?? 0); // 1 0
```

Ownership: key is borrowed. Scalar values copy; owned values from a named receiver are readonly borrows and block mutation or transfer of that receiver while the borrow is in scope. A temporary receiver is consumed and its selected owned value moves out. Use clone() explicitly to own a copy of a borrowed value.

examples.source: const values = new Map<string, int>(); values.set("a", 1); console.log(values.get("a") ?? 0, values.get("missing") ?? 0);

Map.name: has
Map.documentation:
Reports whether a matching key exists, including when its stored value is undefined. Receiver is unchanged.

Keys must match the declared key type. Scalar, enum and union keys are supported; record, array and function identity keys are unsupported. Number keys use SameValueZero: NaN equals NaN, and both zeros are one key. Wrong argument counts or incompatible argument types are static errors.

```tsrust
const values = new Map<string, int>();
values.set("a", 1);
console.log(values.has("a"), values.has("missing")); // true false
```

Ownership: receiver and key are borrowed.

examples.source: const values = new Map<string, int>(); values.set("a", 1); console.log(values.has("a"), values.has("missing"));

Map.name: delete
Map.documentation:
Removes a key and value and returns true, or returns false if absent. Remaining entries keep their order. Deleting and reinserting a key places it last.

Keys must match the declared key type. Scalar, enum and union keys are supported; record, array and function identity keys are unsupported. Number keys use SameValueZero: NaN equals NaN, and both zeros are one key. Wrong argument counts or incompatible argument types are static errors.

```tsrust
const values = new Map<string, int>();
values.set("a", 1);
console.log(values.delete("a"), values.delete("a"), values.size); // true false 0
```

Ownership: key is borrowed; receiver mutates and the removed value is dropped.

examples.source: const values = new Map<string, int>(); values.set("a", 1); console.log(values.delete("a"), values.delete("a"), values.size);

std:fs.name: read

parameters.label: file: Mutable<File | BufferedReader>
parameters.documentation: BufferedReader may read ahead by its capacity. Each call returns at most the currently buffered bytes, or one refill; short reads succeed. Required open file. Exclusively borrowed; a successful read advances its cursor by the returned byte count.

parameters.label: length: int

examples.source: import {open,read,close} from "std:fs"; import {length} from "std:bytes"; function main(){match(open("input.bin")){Ok(file)=>{match(read(file,4)){Ok(bytes)=>{console.log(length(bytes));},Err(error)=>{throw error.message;}}match(close(file)){Ok(_)=>{},Err(error)=>{throw error.message;}}},Err(error)=>{throw error.message;}}}

std:fs.name: close
std:fs.signature: close(file: File | BufferedReader | BufferedWriter): Result<void, FsError>

parameters.label: file: File | BufferedReader | BufferedWriter
parameters.documentation: For BufferedWriter, close first attempts to flush pending bytes, then releases the descriptor even on failure. The first error wins; remaining bytes are discarded without retry. BufferedReader discards unread buffered bytes. Required owned open file. Consumed on both Ok and Err; later use and a second close are source errors.

std:fs.name: write

parameters.label: file: Mutable<File | BufferedWriter>
parameters.documentation: BufferedWriter may accept bytes into memory before any file write. The returned count includes those bytes; flush or close sends pending bytes. An input at least as large as capacity bypasses the buffer after flushing pending bytes. Required writable file. Its cursor advances by the number of bytes successfully written.

parameters.label: bytes: ReadOnly<Bytes | ByteView | ByteViewMut>
parameters.documentation: Required borrowed byte storage, with no additional operation-size ceiling. Views write only their selected range. Storage is not mutated or copied.

examples.source: import {create,write} from "std:fs"; import {fromUtf8} from "std:bytes"; function main(){match(create("output.bin")){Ok(file)=>{match(fromUtf8("ABC")){Ok(bytes)=>{match(write(file,bytes)){Ok(count)=>{console.log(count);},Err(error)=>{throw error.message;}}},Err(error)=>{throw error.message;}}},Err(error)=>{throw error.message;}}}

parameters.label: bytes: ReadOnly<Bytes | ByteView | ByteViewMut>
parameters.documentation: Required borrowed byte storage, with no additional operation-size ceiling. Views write only their selected range. Storage is not mutated or copied.

ThreadPool.documentation:
Creates a lazy task that runs `callback` (optionally receiving a `TaskContext`) on this pool when first awaited. If the pool is full or closed, throws `SpawnError` without waiting. Worker errors, panics and cancellation throw `ThreadError<E>`.

Awaiting does not block other async work. Cancelling before the work starts drops it; after it starts, requests cooperative cancellation and waits for it to stop. A task never awaited submits nothing.

```tsrust
const answer = await pool.taskAsync((): int => 42);
```

Ownership: consumes the callback's captures; results and errors must be owned data.

examples.source: import {ThreadPool} from 'std:threads';async function main():Task<void>{const pool=new ThreadPool({workers:1,capacity:2});const task=pool.taskAsync(():int=>42);console.log(pool.stats().outstanding);console.log(await task);console.log(pool.stats().outstanding);unwrap(pool.shutdown());}

std:http.name: Client

parameters.label: options?: ClientOptions
parameters.documentation: Omit for backend defaults and public CA roots. ca optionally replaces roots with a nonempty PEM bundle; bodyLimit optionally bounds cumulative response bytes. Zero permits empty bodies only. Invalid bounds throw HttpError code options. timeoutMs/connectTimeoutMs optionally set deadlines; followRedirects/maxRedirects control following; proxy/noProxy select proxy behavior. Conflicts and invalid ranges throw options; TLS verification remains enabled.

std:http.documentation:
Creates a reusable HTTP/HTTPS client with connection pooling. With no options it trusts the public CA roots and sets no timeouts or size limits. Defaults: no total request/body timeout and up to 10 redirects.

Optional settings:
- `ca`: a PEM CA bundle that replaces the public roots for this client; certificate and hostname checks stay on. Invalid PEM throws `HttpError` code `tls`.
- `bodyLimit`: maximum bytes per response body (no limit by default); exceeding it throws code `limit`.
- `timeoutMs`, `connectTimeoutMs`: deadlines in milliseconds (none by default).
- `followRedirects`, `maxRedirects`: redirects are followed up to 10 times by default; `followRedirects: false` returns them instead. The two options conflict.
- `proxy`, `noProxy`: set an explicit proxy URL or disable proxies (they conflict); by default the system proxy settings are used.

Invalid values or conflicts throw `HttpError` code `options`. A failure to build the client throws code `client`. Redirect loops throw code `request`. Response decompression and cookies are not handled automatically.

```tsrust
const client = new Client(); // public HTTPS
const privateClient = new Client({
  ca: caPem
}); // private CA only
```

Ownership: borrows `options`; `send` borrows the client until its task finishes.

bodyLimit.documentation:
Explicit cumulative request-byte budget, including multipart framing. Must be positive and target-representable. Content-Length above the budget returns 413; streamed reads fail when the cumulative budget is exceeded. No application byte budget is installed until configure is called.

```tsrust
options.bodyLimit; // 65536 in the service example
```

Ownership: borrows the containing record; clone owned fields when an independent value is needed.

maxConnections.documentation:
Explicit positive, target-representable maximum accepted connections. Additional connections remain in the OS backlog. Construction installs no application connection cap.

```tsrust
options.maxConnections; // 64 in the service example
```

Ownership: borrows the containing record; clone owned fields when an independent value is needed.

maxRequests.documentation:
Explicit positive maximum concurrent handlers, no greater than the backend Semaphore::MAX_PERMITS. Excess arrivals return 503. No application concurrency cap is installed by construction.

```tsrust
options.maxRequests; // 32 in the service example
```

Ownership: borrows the containing record; clone owned fields when an independent value is needed.

requestTimeoutMs.documentation:
Explicit positive handler deadline in milliseconds, representable by the backend monotonic Instant. Expiry requests cancellation and returns 504. It does not bound response streaming after headers. No application handler deadline is installed by construction.

```tsrust
options.requestTimeoutMs; // 5000 in the service example
```

Ownership: borrows the containing record; clone owned fields when an independent value is needed.

shutdownTimeoutMs.documentation:
Explicit positive graceful-connection-drain deadline in milliseconds, representable by the backend monotonic Instant. Expiry cancels remaining connections and drains cleanup. Without configure, graceful shutdown has no application deadline. Native non-yielding work remains cooperative.

```tsrust
options.shutdownTimeoutMs; // 5000 in the service example
```

Ownership: borrows the containing record; clone owned fields when an independent value is needed.

handshakeTimeoutMs.documentation:
Explicit positive TLS handshake deadline in milliseconds, representable by the backend monotonic Instant. Expiry drops the connection. No application handshake deadline is installed by construction; server shutdown still interrupts handshakes.

```tsrust
options.handshakeTimeoutMs; // 3000 in the service example
```

Ownership: borrows the containing record; clone owned fields when an independent value is needed.

requestsPerSecond.documentation:
Explicit nonnegative global arrival budget per fixed one-second window; zero disables it. Excess returns 429. Window boundaries can admit twice this count. No application rate limit is installed by construction.

```tsrust
options.requestsPerSecond; // 100 in the service example
```

Ownership: borrows the containing record; clone owned fields when an independent value is needed.

std:http.name: SseEvent

data.documentation: Required UTF8 event data. Each CR and LF is preserved as a separate backend line separator, so CRLF becomes two data-line breaks. Empty data writes no data field and alone dispatches no browser event. No Tsrust event-size cap is added. The record and its text are consumed when the channel event is encoded.

event.documentation: Optional event name. Omitted writes no event field; a browser treats an absent or empty name as message. CR or LF causes a body error when this queued event is encoded, after any preceding bytes. The record is consumed; the receiver is not mutated.

id.documentation: Optional browser last-event identifier. Omitted writes no id field; empty resets the browser identifier. CR, LF and NUL fail when the body reaches this event. Prior headers cannot be changed. The string moves with its event.

retryMs.documentation: Optional nonnegative retry hint in milliseconds; zero is valid and omission writes no retry field. Negative values fail when this event is encoded. This is a client retry hint; the server does not reconnect. The scalar is consumed with its event.

std:http.name: SseOptions

keepAliveMs.documentation: Optional nonnegative maximum idle interval in milliseconds. Omitted with no text disables keepalive; text alone selects the15-second interval. Zero requests the backend zero interval. An interval outside the timer range throws HttpError code sse during response construction. Options are read and stored independently; no producer is started.

keepAliveText.documentation: Optional keepalive comment text. Supplying text alone enables a15-second interval; an empty string requests an empty comment. Omitted with an interval selects the empty comment. CR or LF throws HttpError code sse before the response is built. The options string is borrowed and copied into the independent transport setting.

std:http.name: WebSocketOptions

readBufferSize.documentation: Optional nonnegative target-representable read-buffer capacity in bytes. Omitted preserves131072 bytes. Zero is accepted by the backend. Invalid values throw HttpError code options before connection or route registration. Configuration is borrowed; each socket owns its buffer.

writeBufferSize.documentation: Optional nonnegative target-representable write-buffer threshold in bytes. Omitted preserves131072 bytes. send flushes its message before its task succeeds. maxWriteBufferSize must exceed this value. Configuration is borrowed; socket buffers remain exclusive owners.

maxWriteBufferSize.documentation: Optional write-buffer maximum in bytes. Omitted preserves the target usize maximum; null explicitly requests that same unbounded backend maximum. A supplied integer must be nonnegative, target-representable and greater than writeBufferSize. Violations throw code options. This bounds the backend buffer, not a new facade queue; configuration is borrowed.

maxMessageSize.documentation: Optional maximum complete incoming message bytes. Omitted preserves67108864 bytes; null disables this backend bound. Integers must be nonnegative and target-representable; zero permits empty messages only. Oversized input fails receive with code capacity. Configuration is borrowed; no message clone is introduced.

maxFrameSize.documentation: Optional maximum incoming frame bytes. Omitted preserves16777216 bytes; null disables this backend bound. Integers must be nonnegative and target-representable. Exceeding the selected bound fails receive with code capacity. Configuration is borrowed and does not install an application queue.

acceptUnmaskedFrames.documentation: Optional server policy for unmasked client frames. Omitted or false preserves rejection; true explicitly permits them. This does not change client masking and is not an origin or authentication check. Configuration is borrowed; install authorization before upgrade.

std:http.name: WebSocketClientOptions

ca.documentation: Optional nonempty PEM CA bundle. Omitted preserves verified public roots. Supplied certificates replace roots for this connection without disabling hostname, chain or validity checks. Invalid PEM throws HttpError code tls. Options remain borrowed until the connect task settles; no key or certificate data is logged.

headers.documentation: Optional ordered request-header entries, including application authorization or origin. Omitted adds none. Invalid header grammar throws code options; handshake rejection throws a transport error with credentials redacted. These are metadata copies, not payload clones. The options array is borrowed through connect settlement.

socket.documentation: Optional socket buffer/frame/message policy. Omitted preserves every backend default. Invalid ranges throw code options before connecting; null message/frame bounds are explicit unlimited policies. The settings are borrowed until connect settles and the resulting socket owns its configuration.

std:http.name: WebSocketHeader

name.documentation: Required HTTP request-header name. Header grammar is checked during connect; invalid names throw HttpError code options. No application header is added by default. The options record is borrowed and the backend request owns parsed metadata.

value.documentation: Required HTTP header value, which may be empty. Invalid control characters throw HttpError code options during connect. Credentials are not included in transport error messages. The header is borrowed and copied as request metadata; no socket payload is cloned.

std:http.name: WebSocketText

kind.documentation: Required text-message tag. It selects UTF8 data and cannot be reassigned to a different message kind. receive retains this tag and send consumes the whole message; the socket is mutated only by the awaited operation.

data.documentation: Required valid UTF8 text, including empty strings and newlines. send consumes the message and flushes; receive returns an independent owned string. No facade size cap is added beyond configured backend limits. The backend byte-to-owned-string conversion may copy a shared receive buffer.

std:http.name: WebSocketBinary

kind.documentation: Required binary-message tag. It preserves binary identity even when the bytes also form valid text. send consumes the record and byte owner; receive creates an independent byte owner. Replacing this tag with text is a type error.

data.documentation: Required owned bytes, including empty payloads. Outgoing storage moves into the backend. Incoming conversion uses the maintained consuming conversion: unique backing storage can transfer, while shared backing storage requires a copy. No borrowed view is silently cloned; pass an owned Bytes value. Configured backend limits still apply.

std:http.name: WebSocketClose

kind.documentation: Required close-message tag. It identifies a received close frame or an explicit outgoing close. It is not ordinary application data; subsequent operations follow the backend closing state. The message is owned and consumed by send or close.

code.documentation: Optional close status. With no code or reason the backend sends a close without a status; a supplied reason alone selects1000. Explicit codes must be allowed16-bit backend close codes. Reserved or invalid codes fail with HttpError code options. Received codes preserve backend protocol-close normalization. The scalar moves with the frame.

reason.documentation: Optional UTF8 close reason. Omission selects no reason; with no code it selects1000. The encoded reason must fit the backend123-byte control-frame range; oversized values fail with code options. receive preserves the actual reason. Text is consumed with the frame; no reconnection is started.

std:http.name: WebSocketHalves

read.documentation: Owned receive half returned by split. It can hold a pending receive while the write half sends. Moving the field transfers that half; it cannot be cloned. Dropping one half leaves the transport retained by the other; both must finish or drop to release it.

write.documentation: Owned sending half returned by split. send waits for backend backpressure and flush. Closing this half sends a close and releases the writer; the reader remains independently owned. The half is moved, never cloned.

HttpApp.name: get
HttpApp.signature: get(path: string, handler: (request: Request) => Task<Response>): void

parameters.label: path: string
parameters.documentation: Absolute route path; literals and :name segments only.

parameters.label: handler: (request: Request) => Task<Response>
parameters.documentation: Named async function or a noncapturing callback returning Task<Response>.

HttpApp.documentation:
Registers a route before listening. Literal paths outrank parameter paths. Parameters remain strings. Duplicate method/path ownership, conflicting parameter names, malformed paths and catch-alls throw HttpError code route. GET also reserves HEAD. Handler failures produce a generic 500; catch errors in the handler for an application-defined response.

```tsrust
app.get("/", handle);
```

Concurrent requests may borrow retained state read-only across await. The handler must own its captures and cannot mutate or consume them. Supported state includes owned configuration and concurrent SQL pools, HTTP clients or async senders. Caller loans, program state, callbacks, local caches and request/body resources cannot be retained. Shutdown drains requests before releasing handlers.

Ownership: mutates the app; each invocation receives its own owned Request.

examples.source: import {App,Client,Request,Response,Body,Next,text,html,json,request,stream} from 'std:http';async function handle(input:Request):Task<Response>{return text('ok');}async function main():Task<void>{const app=new App();app.get("/", handle);console.log('ok');}

HttpApp.name: use
HttpApp.signature: use(middleware: Middleware | ((request: Request, next: Next) => Task<Response>)): void

parameters.label: middleware: Middleware | ((request: Request, next: Next) => Task<Response>)
parameters.documentation: An owned Middleware token, named async function or owned callback. Installation consumes the token/callback; callback captures must own their retained state.

HttpApp.documentation:
Adds middleware that runs for every request, including 404 and 405 responses, in registration order (responses pass back in reverse). Middleware may return early; `next.run` may be called at most once.

```tsrust
app.use(checkRequest);
```

Handlers can share owned state read-only across concurrent requests (configuration, SQL pools, HTTP clients, async senders). Shutdown waits for in-flight requests. Also accepts `Middleware` values from `cors`, `secureHeaders` and `compress`, run in source order; each is used once.

Ownership: each request and `Next` move into the handler call.

examples.source: import {App,Client,Request,Response,Body,Next,text,html,json,request,stream} from 'std:http';async function handle(input:Request):Task<Response>{return text('ok');}async function main():Task<void>{const app=new App();app.use((input:Request,next:Next):Task<Response>=>next.run(input));console.log('ok');}

HttpRequest.name: body
HttpRequest.documentation:
Transfers the unread request body into a streaming reader without performing I/O. No arguments. Reads enforce an explicitly configured request-byte budget; synthetic requests and unconfigured listeners add no byte cap. Excess configured data throws HttpError code limit. For c.req.body(), metadata and Context response helpers remain usable. A second or mixed contextual body read throws code body, even after failure.

```tsrust
const body = c.req.body();
const value = await body.text(); // "hello" for a hello request body
return c.text(value);
```

Ownership: consumes an owned Request. On c.req, mutably borrows the Context only while transferring its body; the returned Body owns the stream.

examples.source: import {App,Client,Request,Response,Body,Next,text,html,json,request,stream} from 'std:http';async function handle(input:Request):Task<Response>{return text('ok');}async function main():Task<void>{const input=request("POST","http://localhost/","hello");const body=input.body();console.log('ok');}

HttpRequest.name: text
HttpRequest.documentation:
Creates a lazy task that collects the body as strict UTF-8 text. No arguments. Body, encoding or configured cumulative byte-budget failures throw HttpError codes body, encoding or limit. Synthetic requests and unconfigured listeners add no byte cap. Suspension does not block a worker.

```tsrust
const value = await input.text(); // "hello"
```

Ownership: consumes the request immediately; disposing its task releases the body.

examples.source: import {App,Client,Request,Response,Body,Next,text,html,json,request,stream} from 'std:http';async function handle(input:Request):Task<Response>{return text('ok');}async function main():Task<void>{const input=request("POST","http://localhost/","hello");const value=await input.text();console.log('ok');}

HttpRequest.name: method
HttpRequest.documentation:
Returns the HTTP method token. No arguments or mutation.

```tsrust
const value = input.method();
```

Ownership: borrows the request.

examples.source: import {App,Client,Request,Response,Body,Next,text,html,json,request,stream} from 'std:http';async function handle(input:Request):Task<Response>{return text('ok');}async function main():Task<void>{const input=request("POST","http://localhost/","hello");const value=input.method();console.log('ok');}

HttpRequest.name: url
HttpRequest.documentation:
Returns the request URI, including its query. Incoming requests normally use a path rather than an absolute URL. No arguments or mutation.

```tsrust
const value = input.url();
```

Ownership: borrows the request.

examples.source: import {App,Client,Request,Response,Body,Next,text,html,json,request,stream} from 'std:http';async function handle(input:Request):Task<Response>{return text('ok');}async function main():Task<void>{const input=request("POST","http://localhost/","hello");const value=input.url();console.log('ok');}

HttpRequest.name: param

parameters.label: name: string
parameters.documentation: Registered :name route parameter.

HttpRequest.documentation:
Returns a decoded route parameter or undefined. Values stay strings; no integer conversion or Unicode normalization. No receiver mutation. Malformed UTF-8 parameters reject the request before the handler.

```tsrust
const id = input.param("id");
```

Ownership: borrows the request and returns independent text.

examples.source: import {App,Client,Request,Response,Body,Next,text,html,json,request,stream} from 'std:http';async function handle(input:Request):Task<Response>{return text('ok');}async function main():Task<void>{const input=request("POST","http://localhost/","hello");const id=input.param("id");console.log('ok');}

HttpRequest.name: form

parameters.label: maxFields?: int
parameters.documentation: Optional nonnegative, target-representable maximum number of fields. Zero permits an empty collection only. Omitted or undefined adds no cardinality cap.

HttpRequest.documentation:
Reads an `application/x-www-form-urlencoded` body when awaited and returns its fields in order, keeping duplicates and empty values. `+` becomes a space and percent escapes are decoded as UTF-8. `maxFields` must be nonnegative; omitted, there is no cardinality cap.

@param maxFields - Optional maximum number of fields; omitted, there is no limit. Negative values throw `HttpError` code `options` before reading.

Malformed content, bad encoding or a body over the configured limit throws `HttpError`.

```tsrust
const fields = await input.form();
```

Ownership: consumes the request; the fields own their data. The body cannot be read again, except that for `c.req` an invalid bound is rejected before reading.

examples.source: import {request} from 'std:http'; async function main():Task<void>{const input=request('POST','http://localhost/', 'a=one+two&a=%C3%A9');input.setHeader('content-type','application/x-www-form-urlencoded');const fields=await input.form();console.log(fields[0].value);console.log(fields[1].value);}

HttpRequest.name: multipart

parameters.label: maxParts?: int
parameters.documentation: Optional nonnegative, target-representable maximum number of parts. Zero permits an empty collection only. Omitted or undefined adds no cardinality cap.

HttpRequest.documentation:
Reads a `multipart/form-data` body when awaited and returns its parts in order, keeping duplicate names and binary data. Each part has a `name`; `fileName` and `contentType` may be `undefined`. `maxParts` must be nonnegative; omitted, there is no cardinality cap.

@param maxParts - Optional maximum number of parts; omitted, there is no limit. Negative values throw `HttpError` code `options` before reading.

File names are untrusted text, never paths. Without a configured body limit the parser caps the body at 2097152 bytes (2 MiB). Malformed content or size failures throw `HttpError`. Nested multipart and streaming to disk are not supported.

```tsrust
const fields = await input.multipart();
```

Ownership: consumes the request; the parts own their data. The body cannot be read again, except that for `c.req` an invalid bound is rejected before reading.

examples.output:
65536 64 32 5000 5000 3000 100
body one two
attachment true true 3

HttpResponse.name: header

parameters.label: name: string
parameters.documentation: HTTP header name.

HttpResponse.documentation:

```tsrust
response.header("x-demo");
```

Ownership: borrows this response.

examples.source: import {App,Client,Request,Response,Body,Next,text,html,json,request,stream} from 'std:http';async function handle(input:Request):Task<Response>{return text('ok');}async function main():Task<void>{const response=text("hello");response.header("x-demo");console.log('ok');}

parameters.label: name: string
parameters.documentation: HTTP header name.

parameters.label: value: string
parameters.documentation: Header value without CR/LF or invalid bytes.

HttpResponse.documentation:
Sets/replaces a header. Invalid names or values throw HttpError code header. Framing headers Content-Length, Transfer-Encoding, Connection and Upgrade are managed by transport and rejected.

```tsrust
response.setHeader("x-demo", "yes");
```

Ownership: mutates this response.

examples.source: import {App,Client,Request,Response,Body,Next,text,html,json,request,stream} from 'std:http';async function handle(input:Request):Task<Response>{return text('ok');}async function main():Task<void>{const response=text("hello");response.setHeader("x-demo", "yes");console.log('ok');}

HttpResponse.name: body
HttpResponse.documentation:
Transfers the unread body into a streaming reader. No arguments. Reading is lazy; this call performs no I/O. Reads enforce ClientOptions.bodyLimit when supplied. Omission adds no response-byte cap.

```tsrust
const body = response.body();
```

Ownership: consumes the response; body cannot be read twice.

examples.source: import {App,Client,Request,Response,Body,Next,text,html,json,request,stream} from 'std:http';async function handle(input:Request):Task<Response>{return text('ok');}async function main():Task<void>{const response=text("hello");const body=response.body();console.log('ok');}

HttpResponse.name: text
HttpResponse.documentation:
Creates a lazy task that collects the body and returns strict UTF-8 text. No arguments. Body, encoding or explicit cumulative byte-budget failures throw HttpError codes body, encoding or limit. Suspension does not block a worker.

```tsrust
const value = await response.text(); // "hello"
```

Ownership: consumes the response immediately; disposing its task releases the body.

examples.source: import {App,Client,Request,Response,Body,Next,text,html,json,request,stream} from 'std:http';async function handle(input:Request):Task<Response>{return text('ok');}async function main():Task<void>{const response=text("hello");const value=await response.text();console.log('ok');}

HttpResponse.name: status
HttpResponse.documentation:
Returns the HTTP response status. No arguments or mutation.

```tsrust
const value = response.status();
```

Ownership: borrows the response.

examples.source: import {App,Client,Request,Response,Body,Next,text,html,json,request,stream} from 'std:http';async function handle(input:Request):Task<Response>{return text('ok');}async function main():Task<void>{const response=text("hello");const value=response.status();console.log('ok');}

HttpServer.name: address
HttpServer.documentation:
Returns the actual bound IP address and port, including the assigned port when listen used port 0. No arguments or mutation.

```tsrust
const address = server.address();
```

Ownership: borrows the server.

examples.source: import {App,Client,Request,Response,Body,Next,text,html,json,request,stream} from 'std:http';async function handle(input:Request):Task<Response>{return text('ok');}async function main():Task<void>{const app=new App();const server=await app.listen("127.0.0.1:0");const address=server.address();await server.shutdown();console.log('ok');}

HttpServer.name: shutdown
HttpServer.documentation:
Creates a lazy shutdown task. Awaiting stops acceptance and gracefully drains active connections. If configure supplied shutdownTimeoutMs, expiry cancels stalled connections before draining nested request tasks. Without configure there is no application drain deadline, so stalled clients or handlers can keep shutdown pending. No arguments. Cleanup may take longer when synchronous application work does not suspend.

```tsrust
await server.shutdown();
```

Ownership: consumes the server; its listener and requests cannot detach.

examples.source: import {App,Client,Request,Response,Body,Next,text,html,json,request,stream} from 'std:http';async function handle(input:Request):Task<Response>{return text('ok');}async function main():Task<void>{const app=new App();const server=await app.listen("127.0.0.1:0");await server.shutdown();console.log('ok');}

HttpServer.name: wait
HttpServer.documentation:
Creates a lazy task that waits for the running listener to finish. Await this at the end of a standalone service to keep its scope alive. No arguments, defaults or receiver reuse. Cancelling or disposing the waiting task requests server shutdown and drains cleanup through its async owner. Source finally is not promised on cancellation.

```tsrust
await server.wait(); // serve until completion or cancellation
```

Ownership: consumes Server immediately; the returned task owns listener cleanup.

examples.source: import {App,Server} from 'std:http';async function keep(server:Server):Task<void>{await server.wait();}async function main():Task<void>{const app=new App();const server=await app.listen('127.0.0.1:0');const running=keep(server).start();running.cancel();try{await running;}catch(error){console.log(error.code);}}

HttpClient.name: send

parameters.label: input: Request
parameters.documentation: Owned request with an absolute HTTP/HTTPS URL and no embedded credentials.

HttpClient.documentation:
Creates a lazy HTTP request task. Awaiting returns response headers and an unread streaming body. HTTP 4xx/5xx are responses, not exceptions. URL and transport failures throw HttpError codes url, request or timeout as reported by the backend. Omitted timeout/redirect/proxy options inherit the selected backend defaults. Explicit ClientOptions override only the selected policies. A total timeout also covers the returned body; expiry during reading throws body. Buffered bodies support backend replay; streaming bodies are not collected or duplicated for replay. Cookies and automatic decompression are not enabled. Use response.text() or body() to read once.

```tsrust
const response = await client.send(request("GET", url, ""));
```

Ownership: consumes the request and borrows the reusable client until completion/disposal.

examples.source: import {App,Client,Request,Response,Body,Next,text,html,json,request,stream} from 'std:http';async function handle(input:Request):Task<Response>{return text('ok');}async function main():Task<void>{const app=new App();const server=await app.listen("127.0.0.1:0");const client=new Client();const response=await client.send(request("GET","http://"+server.address()+"/",""));await server.shutdown();console.log('ok');}

HttpBody.name: next
HttpBody.documentation:
Creates a lazy read of the next data frame. Returns owned bytes, or undefined at end. No arguments. Frame boundaries are transport-dependent; trailers are skipped. Exceeding an explicit cumulative byte budget throws HttpError code limit; transport failures throw body. No background read-ahead is added.

```tsrust
const chunk = await body.next();
```

Ownership: mutably borrows the body until completion/disposal; concurrent reads are rejected.

examples.source: import {App,Client,Request,Response,Body,Next,text,html,json,request,stream} from 'std:http';async function handle(input:Request):Task<Response>{return text('ok');}async function main():Task<void>{const response=text("hello");const body=response.body();const chunk=await body.next();console.log('ok');}

HttpBody.name: text
HttpBody.documentation:
Collects remaining body data as strict UTF-8 text when awaited. No arguments. The remaining cumulative byte budget still applies. Throws HttpError code body, encoding or limit.

```tsrust
const value = await body.text(); // "hello"
```

Ownership: consumes the body; previously read frames are not replayed.

examples.source: import {App,Client,Request,Response,Body,Next,text,html,json,request,stream} from 'std:http';async function handle(input:Request):Task<Response>{return text('ok');}async function main():Task<void>{const response=text("hello");const body=response.body();const value=await body.text();console.log('ok');}

HttpNext.name: run

parameters.label: input: Request
parameters.documentation: Owned request forwarded downstream.

HttpNext.documentation:
Creates a lazy call to remaining middleware and the selected handler. Awaiting returns the downstream response for header changes. Does not restart earlier middleware. No receiver reuse, cloning or second invocation is permitted.

```tsrust
const response = await next.run(input);
```

Ownership: consumes Next and the request immediately, enforcing at-most-once delegation.

examples.source: import {App,Client,Request,Response,Body,Next,text,html,json,request,stream} from 'std:http';async function handle(input:Request):Task<Response>{return text('ok');}async function main():Task<void>{const app=new App();app.use((input:Request,next:Next):Task<Response>=>next.run(input));const server=await app.listen("127.0.0.1:0");const client=new Client();const response=await client.send(request("GET","http://"+server.address()+"/",""));await server.shutdown();console.log('ok');}

parameters.label: value: ReadOnly<Instant>

std:date.documentation:
Returns a new UTC instant at the beginning of the input second, explicitly discarding fractional nanoseconds. Takes one Instant; no defaults and no conversion errors for a valid Instant. The input does not change. This floors toward the earlier instant even before the Unix epoch, rather than truncating an epoch count toward zero. Use before exact Unix conversion only when whole-second resolution is intended.

```tsrust
const value = unwrap(parseISO("1969-12-31T23:59:59.999999999Z"));
toUnixMilliseconds(startOfSecond(value)); // Ok(-1000)
```

Ownership: borrows input and returns an independent owned Instant.

std:crypto.name: sha256

parameters.label: bytes: ReadOnly<Bytes | ByteView | ByteViewMut>
parameters.documentation: Exact bytes to hash, including empty input. Readonly and mutable byte views are accepted without input copying.

std:crypto.documentation:
Hashes exact input bytes with SHA-256 and returns a new 32-byte digest. Empty inputs are valid. No encoding conversion or receiver mutation. Suitable for hashing high-entropy session tokens; this is not a password-hashing function.

```tsrust
const digest = sha256(unwrap(fromUtf8("abc"))); // ba7816bf...f20015ad
```

Ownership: borrows input and returns independent bytes.

std:crypto.documentation:
Compares byte contents using a maintained constant-time primitive for equal-length inputs. Unequal lengths return false; lengths are public and may affect timing. Empty arrays compare equal. Does not make surrounding code or database lookups constant-time.

```tsrust
timingSafeEqual(sha256(unwrap(fromUtf8("abc"))), sha256(unwrap(fromUtf8("abc")))); // true
```

Ownership: borrows both inputs without mutation.

SqlCursor.name: next
close
SqlCursor.documentation:
Disposes a cursor without reading remaining rows. Takes no arguments, returns no value and consumes the cursor. Connection cleanup follows the database driver; pool operations can reuse it once cleanup finishes. Calling close after EOF is allowed; calling any method on the consumed cursor is rejected. Dropping the cursor performs the same cleanup.

```tsrust
const cursor = await db.cursor('SELECT 1 AS value');
cursor.close(); // abandon before reading
```

Ownership: consumes the cursor and releases its pool loan. A pending next() loan must finish or be dropped first.

Interval.name: tick
Interval.documentation:
Creates a lazy wait for the next tick. First tick is immediately ready. Later deadlines follow periodMs and the selected missed-tick behavior. Cancelling a wait does not consume a tick. No arguments or return value.

```tsrust
await timer.tick();
```

Ownership: retains an exclusive timer borrow; finish or dispose this task before another timer operation.

examples.source: import {Interval,MissedTickBehavior} from 'std:futures';async function main():Task<void>{const policy:MissedTickBehavior='skip';const timer=new Interval(1,policy);await timer.tick();console.log('tick');}

CancellationToken.name: share
CancellationToken.documentation:
Returns an explicit handle to the same cancellation signal. Cancel through either handle to wake both sets of waiters. No arguments or ordinary failure.

```tsrust
token.share();
```

Ownership: borrows the token; share and child return explicit owned handles.

examples.source: import {CancellationToken} from 'std:futures';async function main():Task<void>{const token=new CancellationToken();const shared=token.share();const child=token.child();child.cancel();console.log(token.isCancelled(),child.isCancelled());shared.cancel();await token.cancelled();console.log(token.isCancelled());}

CancellationToken.name: child
CancellationToken.documentation:
Returns a descendant signal. Parent cancellation cancels it; cancelling the child does not affect its parent. A child of an already cancelled parent is cancelled immediately. No arguments or ordinary failure.

```tsrust
token.child();
```

Ownership: borrows the token; share and child return explicit owned handles.

examples.source: import {CancellationToken} from 'std:futures';async function main():Task<void>{const token=new CancellationToken();const shared=token.share();const child=token.child();child.cancel();console.log(token.isCancelled(),child.isCancelled());shared.cancel();await token.cancelled();console.log(token.isCancelled());}

CancellationToken.name: cancel
CancellationToken.documentation:
Signals cancellation and wakes current waiters, including descendant tokens. Repeated cancellation is harmless. Does not forcibly stop work; workers must cooperate. No arguments or return value.

```tsrust
token.cancel();
```

Ownership: borrows the token; share and child return explicit owned handles.

examples.source: import {CancellationToken} from 'std:futures';async function main():Task<void>{const token=new CancellationToken();const shared=token.share();const child=token.child();child.cancel();console.log(token.isCancelled(),child.isCancelled());shared.cancel();await token.cancelled();console.log(token.isCancelled());}

CancellationToken.name: isCancelled
CancellationToken.documentation:
Returns whether this signal has been cancelled. No arguments, mutation or ordinary failure; concurrent cancellation may change the answer immediately.

```tsrust
token.isCancelled();
```

Ownership: borrows the token; share and child return explicit owned handles.

examples.source: import {CancellationToken} from 'std:futures';async function main():Task<void>{const token=new CancellationToken();const shared=token.share();const child=token.child();child.cancel();console.log(token.isCancelled(),child.isCancelled());shared.cancel();await token.cancelled();console.log(token.isCancelled());}

CancellationToken.name: cancelled
CancellationToken.documentation:
Creates a lazy wait for cancellation. Already cancelled signals return immediately when awaited. Cancelling the waiting task leaves the token unchanged. No arguments or return value.

```tsrust
await token.cancelled();
```

Ownership: borrows the token until the wait completes or is disposed.

examples.source: import {CancellationToken} from 'std:futures';async function main():Task<void>{const token=new CancellationToken();const shared=token.share();const child=token.child();child.cancel();console.log(token.isCancelled(),child.isCancelled());shared.cancel();await token.cancelled();console.log(token.isCancelled());}

std:ui.name: LazyChildren
Svg

parameters.label: props: SvgProps<ReactiveValue<string>, ReactiveValue<string>>
parameters.documentation: Optional owned Path children, viewBox, width/height, aspect policy, paint and element metadata. Defaults to a decorative 24px viewport. Classes and variant metadata may be live. See SvgProps for exact fields and errors.

std:ui.documentation:
A vector image drawn from `Path` children in paint order.

- Defaults: `viewBox="0 0 24 24"`, 24 by 24, `fill="currentColor"`, `stroke="none"`.
- Add `aria-label` for meaningful images; without it the image is decorative.
- Theme colors and `currentColor` follow the current theme. Gradients, filters, masks and other SVG elements are not supported; invalid geometry or paint throws.

Ownership: consumes its props and `Path` children.

```tsrx
<Svg viewBox="0 0 24 24" width={32} height={32} stroke="primary" fill="none" strokeWidth={2}>
  <Path d="M3 12h18M12 3v18"/>
</Svg>
```

examples.source: import {Svg,Path,document} from 'std:ui';import {strictEqual} from 'std:testing';function main(){const html=document(<Svg aria-label="Saved" fill="none" stroke="currentColor"><Path d="M2 12L10 20L22 4"/></Svg>,'Vector');strictEqual(html.includes('role="img"'),true);strictEqual(html.includes('d="M2 12L10 20L22 4"'),true);console.log('Vector markup passed');}

std:ui.name: Path

parameters.label: props: PathProps<ReactiveValue<string>, ReactiveValue<string>, ReactiveValue<string>>
parameters.documentation: Required d accepts a string or automatic live scalar expression. Optional paint overrides Svg; optional classes support base text colors/opacity only. Path requires an enclosing Svg and has no children.

std:ui.documentation:
One shape inside an `Svg`, from SVG path data (`M L H V C S Q T A Z`, absolute or relative).

- An empty `d` draws nothing; malformed data throws.
- Paint inherits from the `Svg` unless set here. Layout classes belong on the `Svg`.
- Changing `d` redraws the same path.

Ownership: consumes its props.

```tsrx
<Svg viewBox="0 0 24 24"><Path d="M2 12L10 20L22 4" stroke="destructive" fill="none"/></Svg>
```

std:ui.name: SvgProps
std:ui.documentation:
Vector viewport options. Omitted scalar fields use the documented defaults; paint and viewport are construction-time snapshots. Accessible metadata supports declared live bindings. Classes/Variant default to string for local wrapper compatibility; select ReactiveValue<string> for live wrappers. No receiver methods or mutation. Ownership: component calls consume these records and children.

```tsrx
<Svg viewBox="0 0 24 24" width={48} height={48} className="text-primary"><Path d="M12 2l3 7h7l-5.5 4.5 2 7.5-6.5-4.5-6.5 4.5 2-7.5L2 9h7z"/></Svg>
```

id.documentation: Optional document identifier, without ASCII whitespace or control characters. Defaults to none. <View id="account" /> produces id="account" in HTML. Both adapters retain it as tree metadata; no lookup or routing API is created. Construction throws for invalid IDs. Ownership: consumes the supplied string.

aria-label.documentation: Optional constant or live vector-image name. Omission or undefined defaults to decorative presentation with aria-hidden=true; a nonempty name defaults to role=img and aria-hidden=false. These automatic defaults follow the current label after handlers. Explicit role/aria-hidden overrides remain checked: visible image semantics require a nonempty name and presentation cannot be named. <Svg aria-label={saved.get() ? "Saved" : undefined}>…</Svg> changes semantics without replacing geometry. Ownership: transfers the string or weak state evaluator once.

aria-hidden.documentation: Optional constant or live accessibility exclusion. Undefined follows the current SVG label: true for an unlabelled decorative image, false for a named image. It changes accessibility rather than paint. A visible role=img requires a nonempty name. Ownership: transfers the boolean or weak state evaluator once.

data-slot.documentation: Optional component slot name, using only ASCII letters, digits and hyphens. Defaults to none. <View data-slot="card-content" /> emits that HTML attribute and retains the same native metadata. Invalid names throw. Checked data/descendant/group selectors can match this metadata; arbitrary CSS selectors remain unsupported. Ownership: consumes the slot string.

data-size.documentation: Optional component size metadata using ASCII letters, digits and hyphens; defaults to absent. <View data-size="sm" className="data-[size=sm]:p-3" /> uses the small metadata condition on both targets. The string does not select dimensions by itself or add an accessibility role. Invalid characters throw. No function arguments. Ownership: consumes the supplied string.

aria-describedby.documentation: Optional constant or live space-separated document IDs; undefined or empty removes the relationship. <Input aria-describedby={invalid.get() ? "error" : "hint"}/> exposes the current referenced text as its accessible description on both targets. Missing IDs are ignored and order is preserved. This does not name the control or run validation. Control characters other than ASCII whitespace reject. Ownership: transfers the ID string or evaluator once; state captures remain weak.

aria-invalid.documentation: Optional constant or live boolean describing validation state. <Input aria-invalid={invalid.get() ? true : undefined}/> adds invalid styling and accessibility when true; undefined removes the explicit state and false states valid. No validation runs and the field value stays unchanged. Both adapters refresh the same retained control after handlers. Ownership: transfers the flag or evaluator once without retaining component state owners.

data-variant.documentation: Optional variant metadata, default absent. ASCII letters, digits and hyphens are accepted; empty omits the attribute. This does not choose styles or change accessibility by itself. Example: <View data-variant="destructive" className="data-[variant=destructive]:text-destructive" /> selects the destructive text token on both targets. Invalid characters throw. Plain string props remain construction-time snapshots. Direct state-reading intrinsic TSRX expressions update after handlers without remounting. Custom components need an explicit reactive prop contract; precomputed values remain snapshots. Ownership: transfers one string or owned evaluator once; bindings do not retain component state owners.

fill.documentation: Fill paint: none, currentColor, a semantic token name, checked hex or in-gamut oklch. Svg defaults to currentColor; Path inherits. External paint URLs are rejected. Example: <Svg fill="primary"><Path d="M0 0H24V24H0Z"/></Svg> fills a square with primary. none disables fill; paint URLs and unsupported CSS color formats throw. Native layout/GPU floating precision and rasterization apply; source data is not changed. Ownership: consumes props and strings without cloning nodes.

stroke.documentation: Stroke paint with the same accepted values as fill. Svg defaults to none; Path inherits. Example: <Svg fill="none" stroke="currentColor"><Path d="M2 12L22 12"/></Svg> strokes a line in inherited text color. none disables the stroke. Native layout/GPU floating precision and rasterization apply; source data is not changed. Ownership: consumes props and strings without cloning nodes.

strokeWidth.documentation: Finite nonnegative stroke width in viewBox units. Svg defaults to 1; Path inherits. Native geometry precision applies. Example: <Svg stroke="primary" strokeWidth={2}><Path d="M2 12L22 12"/></Svg> uses two viewBox units, two logical pixels at the default size. Zero disables stroking. Negative, NaN, infinite or native-overflow values throw before JSON serialization. Native layout/GPU floating precision and rasterization apply; source data is not changed. Ownership: consumes props and strings without cloning nodes.

strokeLinecap.documentation: End-cap geometry. Svg defaults to butt; Path inherits. Example: <Svg stroke="primary" strokeWidth={2} strokeLinecap="round"><Path d="M2 12L22 12"/></Svg> extends rounded caps one unit past each endpoint. butt stops at endpoints; square extends square caps. Other values throw. Native layout/GPU floating precision and rasterization apply; source data is not changed. Ownership: consumes props and strings without cloning nodes.

strokeLinejoin.documentation: Join geometry. Svg defaults to miter; Path inherits. Example: <Svg stroke="primary" fill="none" strokeLinejoin="round"><Path d="M2 20L12 2L22 20"/></Svg> rounds the corner. miter observes strokeMiterlimit; bevel cuts the corner. Other values throw. Native layout/GPU floating precision and rasterization apply; source data is not changed. Ownership: consumes props and strings without cloning nodes.

strokeMiterlimit.documentation: Finite miter length/width limit, at least 1. Svg defaults to 4; Path inherits. Example: <Svg stroke="primary" strokeMiterlimit={1}><Path d="M2 20L12 2L22 20"/></Svg> bevels a join beyond that unitless length/width ratio. Values below 1, nonfinite or native-overflow values throw, even with another join style. Native layout/GPU floating precision and rasterization apply; source data is not changed. Ownership: consumes props and strings without cloning nodes.

fillRule.documentation: Interior winding rule. Svg defaults to nonzero; Path inherits. Example: <Svg fillRule="evenodd"><Path d="M0 0H24V24H0Z M6 6H18V18H6Z"/></Svg> leaves a center hole; nonzero fills both same-direction contours. Other values throw. Native layout/GPU floating precision and rasterization apply; source data is not changed. Ownership: consumes props and strings without cloning nodes.

viewBox.documentation: Four finite x/y/width/height numbers separated by spaces or commas. Width/height must be positive. Defaults to 0 0 24 24. Example: <Svg viewBox="10 20 40 20" width={96} height={96}/> maps (10,20) to viewport (0,24) with centered meet. Negative origins work. Empty numbers, zero/negative extents, nonfinite/native-overflow values or transforms throw. Native layout/GPU floating precision and rasterization apply; source data is not changed. Ownership: consumes props and strings without cloning nodes.

width.documentation: Preferred viewport width in logical pixels. Finite and nonnegative; defaults to 24. Width utilities override this value. Example: <Svg width={48} height={24}/> prefers 48px width; className="w-16" overrides it to 64px with default spacing. Zero paints nothing; negative, NaN, infinite or native-overflow dimensions throw. No focus is added. Native layout/GPU floating precision and rasterization apply; source data is not changed. Ownership: consumes props and strings without cloning nodes.

height.documentation: Preferred viewport height in logical pixels. Finite and nonnegative; defaults to 24. Height utilities override this value. Example: <Svg width={48} height={24}/> prefers 24px height; className="h-16" overrides it to 64px with default spacing. Zero paints nothing; negative, NaN, infinite or native-overflow dimensions throw. Native layout/GPU floating precision and rasterization apply; source data is not changed. Ownership: consumes props and strings without cloning nodes.

preserveAspectRatio.documentation: none stretches independently. xMin/Mid/MaxYMin/Mid/Max plus optional meet/slice aligns a uniform scale. Defaults to xMidYMid meet. Example: <Svg viewBox="0 0 40 20" width={96} height={96} preserveAspectRatio="xMidYMid meet"/> centers a 96 by 48 drawing. none stretches both axes. slice fills the viewport and may clip. All nine alignments work; extra/unknown words reject. Stroke scales with geometry; non-scaling stroke is unsupported. Native layout/GPU floating precision and rasterization apply; source data is not changed. Ownership: consumes props and strings without cloning nodes.

role.documentation: Image semantics. Named images default to img; unlabelled icons default to presentation and aria-hidden. Visible images require aria-label. Example: <Svg aria-label="Sales"/> exposes one image named Sales. Explicit img without a label stays hidden by default; aria-hidden=false then requires a label. presentation cannot be named. No action or keyboard focus is added. Native layout/GPU floating precision and rasterization apply; source data is not changed. Ownership: consumes props and strings without cloning nodes.

children.documentation: Owned Path nodes in paint order. Other node/text children reject. An empty d hides a retained path. Example: <Svg><Path d="M2 2L22 22"/><Path d="M22 2L2 22"/></Svg> paints the second path last. Text, controls, nested Svg and branch wrappers reject. Use live empty d to hide a retained shape. Children transfer once. Native layout/GPU floating precision and rasterization apply; source data is not changed. Ownership: consumes props and strings without cloning nodes.

className.documentation: Shared box and color utilities. Defaults to empty. Svg starts at 24 by 24 and clips to its viewport; overflow-visible opts out. Intrinsic auto/fit sizing rejects; use explicit, fractional or viewport dimensions. Example: <Svg className="size-6 text-primary"/> is 24px at default spacing and passes primary as currentColor. <Path className="text-destructive opacity-50" d="M2 2L22 22"/> uses destructive with half subtree opacity. Put layout, interaction styles and theme scopes on Svg; Path rejects them. Native layout/GPU floating precision and rasterization apply; source data is not changed. Ownership: consumes props and strings without cloning nodes.

std:ui.name: Route

parameters.label: props: RouteProps
parameters.documentation: path is an absolute local path. exact defaults to true. render is an owned zero-argument factory returning Node, called once on first match.

std:ui.documentation:
Shows its content while the location matches `path`, building it the first time it matches.

- Create a `location()` or `createLocation()` owner in the window root first.
- `path` takes named segments such as `/users/:id`. `exact` defaults to true; `exact={false}` also matches deeper paths (`/docs` matches `/docs/api`).
- Content built once is kept, with its state and scroll position, when the route is left and revisited.

Ownership: consumes `render`; visited content lives until the parent is disposed.

```tsrx
const path = location();
<Route path="/docs" render={() => <Text>Documentation</Text>}/>
```
