std:ui.name: RouteProps
std:ui.documentation:
Properties for retained, lazy route content. Supply path and render; exact defaults to true. Only a matching route calls its factory. For example, <Route path="/docs" exact={false} render={() => <Text>Docs</Text>}/> matches /docs and /docs/api. Ownership: transfers the factory once; constructed content remains owned by its route.

```tsrx
<Route path="/settings" exact={false} render={() => <Settings/>}/>
```

path.documentation: Required absolute local route path. Trailing slashes normalize. Queries, escapes, traversal and heading fragments throw. Example: path="/docs" matches /docs, including /docs#heading. Read at construction; changing an ordinary prop record does not update the path. Ownership: copies the checked path into the route. Named segments such as /users/:id match one nonempty segment. Names must be unique ASCII identifiers. Read their values with routeParam(path.get(), pattern, name).

exact.documentation: Optional boolean, default true. false matches the path and its descendants at slash boundaries. Example: path="/docs" exact={false} matches /docs/api and rejects /docs-other. / with exact=false matches all local paths. Fragments do not affect matching. Ownership: copies one boolean at construction.

render.documentation: Required owned zero-argument function returning Node. Runs once on the first match. Example: render={() => <Text>Hello</Text>} constructs Hello only after its route becomes active. Revisits keep the same subtree and state. Errors propagate; no automatic retry. Ownership: consumes the factory and releases captures after its call; uncalled factories and visited subtrees release with the parent.

std:ui.name: Link

parameters.label: props: LinkProps<ReactiveValue<string>, ReactiveValue<string>>
parameters.documentation: href is an absolute application path or HTTPS URL without credentials. disabled (boolean or live condition, default false) dims the link and ignores clicks. children contains owned phrasing content; className defaults to empty. Element identity and naming are forwarded.

std:ui.documentation:
A link. Local paths such as `/docs` or `/docs#heading` navigate in the window; `https://` URLs open the default browser.

- Create the window's location owner before local links.
- The current page gets `aria-current` (`page`, or `location` for a parent path); style it with `aria-current:` classes.
- Other schemes (`http:`, `file:`, `javascript:`) and malformed paths throw. `disabled` dims the link and ignores activation.

Ownership: consumes its children.

```tsrx
<Link href="/docs">Docs</Link>
<Link href="https://github.com/Forever-Frameworks-LLC/tsrust">GitHub</Link>
```

std:ui.name: location
std:ui.documentation:
Creates the window's location (the current local path), starting at `/`.

- `get()` returns the path; `set(path)` navigates and records history; `back()` and `forward()` move through it.
- Setting the current path again adds no history entry.
- Create one, as a `const` in the root component; a second one in the same window throws.

Ownership: the component owns the location; links and handlers do not keep it alive.

```tsrx
const path = location();
<Text>Current page: {path}</Text> // Current page: /
```

std:ui.name: createLocation

parameters.label: initial?: string
parameters.documentation: Initial checked absolute local path, default '/'. Trailing slashes normalize; queries, escapes, traversal and empty fragments throw.

std:ui.name: routeParam
std:ui.signature: routeParam(path: string, pattern: string, name: string): string

parameters.label: path: string
parameters.documentation: Current checked absolute local path. Pass path.get() inside a reactive expression to follow navigation. A heading fragment does not affect matching.

parameters.label: pattern: string
parameters.documentation: Complete route pattern, such as '/teams/:team/users/:user'. Named segments start with ':' and use unique ASCII identifier names. Queries, escapes, traversal and fragments throw.

parameters.label: name: string
parameters.documentation: Parameter name without ':', such as 'user'. Returns an empty string if this parameter is absent or the complete pattern does not match.

std:ui.documentation:
Reads one named segment of `path` matched against `pattern`.

Returns the segment, or an empty string when the whole pattern does not match or has no such name. `routeParam('/users/ada', '/users/:id', 'id')` returns `'ada'`. Fragments are ignored; percent escapes and malformed patterns throw.

Ownership: borrows its arguments and returns a new string.

```tsrx
<Text>{routeParam(path.get(), '/users/:id', 'id')}</Text>
```

std:ui.name: navigate

parameters.label: path: string
parameters.documentation: Absolute application path with an optional nonempty heading fragment. The local path restrictions of Link apply; HTTPS links cannot be passed to navigate.

std:ui.documentation:
Pushes an application location and updates shared route bindings. Returns void; does not mutate the argument. The current path is a no-op. A missing/disposed location owner or invalid path throws. Example: navigate("/docs"); makes location().get() /docs on the existing owner; do not create another location owner to read it. Ownership: borrows the path and retains no state owner.

```tsrx
<Button onPress={() => { navigate('/settings'); }}>Settings</Button>
```

std:ui.name: back
std:ui.documentation:
Visits the previous application history entry. No arguments; returns void. Native history stops at its initial entry. A missing/disposed location owner throws. Example: navigate("/docs"); back(); restores / on a new native application. Ownership: retains no location or route subtree.

```tsrx
<Button onPress={() => { back(); }}>Back</Button>
```

std:ui.name: forward
std:ui.documentation:
Visits the next application history entry after back(). No arguments; returns void. The location updates immediately. Native history with no next entry is unchanged. A missing/disposed location owner throws. Example: navigate("/docs"); back(); forward(); restores /docs on native. Ownership: retains no location or route subtree.

```tsrx
<Button onPress={() => { forward(); }}>Forward</Button>
```

std:ui.name: CopyButton

parameters.label: props: CopyButtonProps<ReactiveValue<string>, ReactiveValue<string>>
parameters.documentation: value is the exact text to copy, including Unicode, CRLF and trailing whitespace. className defaults to empty; normal element identity and accessible naming props apply.

std:ui.documentation:
A copy icon button. Activating it writes value to the system clipboard and briefly shows a check mark; an empty string clears the clipboard's text.

```tsrx
<CopyButton value="npm install tsrust"/>
```

After a click the clipboard holds exactly npm install tsrust. Ownership: consumes props and owns a text snapshot.

std:ui.name: CopyButtonProps
std:ui.documentation:
Clipboard button properties. value is required; className and inherited ElementProps are optional. Ownership: consumes the value and other supplied strings.

```tsrx
<CopyButton value="npm install tsrust"/>
```

value.documentation: Required string copied exactly, including Unicode, newlines and whitespace. No trimming or numeric conversion. <CopyButton value="hello"/> copies hello on activation. Empty text is supported. Ownership: stores an independent snapshot.

className.documentation: Optional checked shared button utilities, default empty. <CopyButton value="hello" className="rounded border px-3 py-2"/> styles the control on both targets. Unknown utilities throw. Shared aspect utilities set a preferred width/height ratio: aspect-square (1), aspect-video (16/9), aspect-[W/H], aspect-[R], or aspect-auto. Ratios must be finite, positive and within f32 native layout range; both targets use the normalized f32 ratio. With default spacing, <View className="w-64 aspect-video"/> is 256 by 144 logical pixels. Explicit width and height and min/max bounds take precedence. Children can overflow without clipping. Every UI layout box establishes a containing block. absolute removes a box from flow and positions it in its immediate UI parent; relative keeps normal flow. Insets use checked theme spacing, fractions/full or auto. Inline descendants reject box utilities. fixed/sticky positioning, z-index and transforms remain unsupported. Direct state-reading intrinsic TSRX expressions update after handlers without remounting. Custom components need an explicit reactive prop contract; precomputed values remain snapshots. Ownership: transfers one string or owned evaluator once; bindings do not retain component state owners. Text flow supports whitespace-normal/nowrap/pre/pre-wrap; nowrap collapses spaces without soft wraps. underline/no-underline controls local decoration, and underline-offset-auto/0/1/2/4/8 selects font metrics or logical pixels below the baseline. Ancestor decorations remain. rounded-2xl/3xl/4xl uses 1.25/1.5/2 times radius.xl, with lg fallback. [a]: variants apply only to a Link. Stored text and editable values remain unchanged.

std:ui.name: Text

parameters.label: props: TextProps<ReactiveValue<string>, ReactiveValue<string>>
parameters.documentation: Optional children is an ordered Child array: scalar text/bindings and inline Text or Link nodes. Null/undefined are omitted. className defaults to empty.

std:ui.documentation:
Text from strings, numbers and signals, in order. Signal values and expressions that read component state update after each handler, without rerunning the component.

- `variant="secondary"` (or `muted`) uses the muted color.
- `as` picks the element: `span` (default), `div`, `p`, `h1`–`h6`, `code`, `kbd`, `strong`, `em` or `del`.
- `null` and `undefined` children show nothing. Nested `Text` and `Link` wrap as one paragraph.
- Text can be selected and copied with the usual shortcuts.

Ownership: consumes its props; bindings do not keep state alive.

```tsrx
const count = signal(0);
<Text className="text-lg font-semibold">Count: {count}</Text> // Count: 0
```

std:ui.name: View

parameters.label: props: ViewProps<ReactiveValue<string>, ReactiveValue<string>>
parameters.documentation: Optional children is an ordered Child array: text strings/numbers, Signal/TextBinding values, owned Nodes, null or undefined. Omission defaults to empty. className defaults to empty.

std:ui.documentation:
A layout container for text and child nodes, styled with utility classes (flex, grid, spacing, sizing, colors).

- `as` picks the element, such as `div` (default), `section`, `nav`, `main`, `ul`/`li` or `table`/`tr`/`td`; landmark, list and table roles are kept.
- A ternary that reads component state (`{open.get() ? <Panel/> : null}`) builds only the chosen branch.
- `hidden` hides a subtree but keeps its state; `tabIndex={0}` makes it focusable; `overflow-auto` scrolls.
- Responsive `sm:` to `2xl:` and `dark:` variants work. Arbitrary CSS does not; unknown utilities throw.

Ownership: consumes its props and children.

```tsrx
<View className="flex-col gap-4 p-6">
  <Text>Title</Text>
  <Button>Continue</Button>
</View>
```

std:ui.name: Button

parameters.label: props: ButtonProps<ReactiveValue<string>, ReactiveValue<string>>
parameters.documentation: Optional children accepts strings/numbers, Signal/TextBinding values and owned phrasing Nodes, null or undefined. disabled defaults to false and also accepts compiler-derived ReactiveBoolean conditions. onPress is optional. className defaults to empty.

std:ui.documentation:
A focusable button. `onPress` runs once per click, Enter or Space.

- Children are text, signals and inline elements such as `Text`, `code` or `kbd`; nested controls throw.
- `variant` and size presets come from GPUI Kit; utility classes adjust or restyle it.
- `disabled` (including a live condition such as `disabled={busy.get()}`) blocks activation and focus.
- `aria-label` sets the accessible name.

Ownership: consumes its children and handler.

```tsrx
const count = signal(0);
<Button onPress={() => { count.set(count.get() + 1); }}>Clicked {count}</Button>
```

std:ui.name: document

parameters.label: node: ReadOnly<Node>
parameters.documentation: Tree to render, borrowed without modification.

parameters.label: title: string
parameters.documentation: Document title; HTML metacharacters are escaped.

std:ui.documentation:
Produces a complete semantic HTML document with the shared utility styles. Escapes text and title, preserving Unicode. Does not open a window, execute handlers or mutate nodes. Example: document(<Text>Hello</Text>, "Demo") returns HTML containing an escaped title and a span labelled Hello. Ownership: borrows the tree and title; returns an independent owned string.

```tsrx
const html = document(<Text>Hello</Text>, 'Demo');
console.log(html.includes('Hello')); // true
```

std:ui.signature: run(node: Node, title: string, options?: WindowOptions): Result<void, UiError>

parameters.label: node: Node
parameters.documentation: Owned tree displayed until window closure; consumed even if startup fails.

parameters.label: title: string
parameters.documentation: Native window title, borrowed during setup.

parameters.label: options?: WindowOptions
parameters.documentation: Optional creation-time dimensions and native/custom titlebar. Defaults to 640×480 logical pixels, minimum 240×160, native titlebar. Invalid dimensions return Err.

std:ui.name: signal
std:ui.documentation:
Creates component state holding a scalar, nullable value, array or plain record.

- `get()` returns a copy; `set(next)` replaces the value and updates everything that shows it.
- Editing a copy changes nothing until you `set` it.
- Declare it with `const` in a component. Resources, borrowed views and callbacks cannot be stored.

Ownership: the returned component tree owns the state; bindings and handlers do not keep it alive.

```tsrx
const name = signal('Ada');
<Input value={name.get()} onChange={(event) => { name.set(clone(event.target.value)); }}/>
<Text>Hello, {name}</Text>
```

parameters.label: initial: T
parameters.documentation: Required scalar, nullable value, array or plain data record. Nested data is copied independently into state; there is no default value. Resources, borrowed views and callbacks are rejected.

std:ui.name: Node
Signal
std:ui.documentation:
Component state created by `signal(initial)`; see `signal`.

- `get()` returns a copy; `set(next)` replaces the value and updates bound text.
- Scalar signals can be used directly as text children. For a live field of a record or array, use `computed<T>(() => state.get().field)`.
- Reading a disposed signal throws `UiError`. Signals cannot be cloned or sent to threads.

Ownership: one component owns it; bindings do not keep it alive.

```tsrx
const open = signal(false);
<Switch checked={open.get()} onChange={(on) => { open.set(on); }}/>
```

std:ui.name: UiError
std:ui.documentation:
A UI failure with string code and message fields. run returns Err for renderer or handler failures and releases its owned subtree. Example: const result = run(node, "Demo"); returns Result<void, UiError>. Errors own their message; no renderer resource is retained.

```tsrx
match (run(<App/>, 'App')) {
  Ok(_) => {},
  Err(error) => { console.log(error.message); },
}
```

std:ui.name: WindowOptions
std:ui.documentation:
Settings for `run`, read when the window opens.

`width`, `height`, `minWidth` and `minHeight` are logical pixels (defaults 640 by 480, minimums 240 by 160; minimums cannot exceed the initial size). `titlebar: "custom"` hides the system title bar but keeps the window controls (macOS only). `fonts` lists `.ttf`/`.otf` files to load and `font` sets the default family. Invalid options make `run` return `Err`.

Ownership: plain settings data, consumed by `run`.

```tsrx
run(<App/>, 'Docs', { width: 1040, height: 760, minWidth: 480, font: 'Inter', fonts: ['fonts/Inter.ttf'] });
```

width.documentation: Initial content width, 240–16384 logical pixels; defaults to 640. Invalid values return Err from run. Ownership: reads ordinary configuration during setup.

height.documentation: Initial content height, 160–16384 logical pixels; defaults to 480. Invalid values return Err from run. Ownership: reads ordinary configuration during setup.

minWidth.documentation: Minimum content width, 240–initial width; defaults to 240. Invalid values return Err from run. Ownership: reads ordinary configuration during setup.

minHeight.documentation: Minimum content height, 160–initial height; defaults to 160. Invalid values return Err from run. Ownership: reads ordinary configuration during setup.

titlebar.documentation: Native (default) or custom. Custom currently requires macOS and preserves traffic-light controls. Reserve header space and mark View drag regions. Other desktop platforms return Err. Creation-time only, not a live mode. Invalid values return Err from run. Ownership: reads ordinary configuration during setup.

std:ui.name: withTheme
std:ui.signature: withTheme<T>(node: Node, value: ReadOnly<T>, mode?: string | Signal<string>): Node

parameters.label: node: Node
parameters.documentation: The owned subtree receiving this theme scope.

parameters.label: value: T
parameters.documentation: Serializable project theme data checked against the theme schema, normally read from tsrust.config.json ui.theme. Borrowed only during this call.

parameters.label: mode?: string | Signal<string>
parameters.documentation: Light or dark, default light. A string Signal switches mode after handlers while preserving child state, fields and identities. Invalid strings throw. This binding retains no state owner.

std:ui.documentation:
Applies a project theme (colors, spacing, radius, type sizes) to a subtree.

- `value` needs every light and dark color token; colors are `#RRGGBB`, `#RRGGBBAA`, `oklch(...)` or `@token` aliases. Missing or invalid tokens throw.
- `mode` is `"light"` or `"dark"`, or a string signal to switch at runtime without rebuilding the subtree.
- Nested themes stay independent.

Ownership: consumes the node; the theme is read once when the subtree is built.

```tsrx
import theme from './theme.json'; // a complete ThemeConfig
const mode = signal('light');
const node = withTheme(<App/>, theme, mode); // mode.set('dark') switches palettes
```

std:ui.name: ThemeConfig

schemaVersion.documentation: Theme schema identifier. Must be int 1; other values fail validation. Read with theme.schemaVersion; the bundled theme returns 1. Reading does not change the theme. Ownership: copies the scalar.

light.documentation: Semantic colors selected by light mode, the default mode of withTheme. Surface ThemeColors keys are required; syntaxKeyword/String/Number/Type have built-in defaults. For the bundled theme, theme.light.primary is the raw string #2563eb. Reading does not resolve aliases or mutate data. Ownership: borrows the color record.

dark.documentation: Semantic colors selected by withTheme(node, theme, "dark"). Surface ThemeColors keys are required; syntaxKeyword/String/Number/Type have built-in defaults. The bundled theme.dark.background is #0f172a. Reading does not mutate data. Ownership: borrows the color record.

spacing.documentation: Required sm/md/lg spacing scale, 0–512 finite logical pixels per value. p-2/4/6, px-, py- and gap- use these slots; 0 uses zero. theme.spacing.md is 16 in the bundled theme. Both adapters apply display scaling. Ownership: borrows the scale; reading does not mutate it.

radius.documentation: Required sm/md/lg corner scale, 0–256 finite logical pixels. rounded uses md; rounded-sm/lg use the other slots. The bundled theme.radius.md is 8, including rounded button focus geometry. Ownership: borrows the scale; reading does not mutate it. Optional xl selects extra-large corners; omitted falls back to lg.

typography.documentation: Required base/xl text sizes, 8–128 finite logical pixels. text-base/xl select these sizes. theme.typography.xl is 24 in the bundled theme. text-sm derives 14px/20px at base=16. Generic font-sans/serif/mono utilities select platform families; custom named font assets remain unsupported. Ownership: borrows the scale; reading does not mutate it.

Functional conversion uses renderer float precision; native paint uses 8-bit sRGB. For example, background: "#123456" resolves to sRGB bytes 18, 52, 86. sm.documentation: Required sm scale slot. Finite int or number logical pixels: spacing 0–512; radius 0–256. For the bundled theme, theme.spacing.sm is 8 and theme.radius.sm is 4. No missing-value default. Reading leaves the receiver unchanged. Ownership: copies the scalar value.

std:ui.name: ThemeTypography
std:ui.documentation:
Required base/xl text dimensions, 8–128 finite logical pixels, plus optional headingFamily. Base/xl have no missing-value defaults; headingFamily defaults to sans. Text inherits its enclosing theme. font-heading selects the scoped heading family. Ownership: ordinary data; reading does not mutate it.

```tsrx
const typography: ThemeTypography = { base: 16, xl: 24, headingFamily: 'serif' };
```

base.documentation: Required base text size, int or number between 8 and 128 logical pixels. theme.typography.base is 16 in the bundled theme. Reading returns that scalar without changing the receiver. Ownership: copies the scalar value.

xl.documentation: Required xl text size, int or number between 8 and 128 logical pixels. theme.typography.xl is 24 in the bundled theme. Reading returns that scalar without changing the receiver. Ownership: copies the scalar value.

headingFamily.documentation: Optional generic heading font family: sans (default), serif or mono. font-heading applies it on both targets; explicit font-sans/serif/mono can override it. Named font files and other values reject. Example: const typography: ThemeTypography = { base: 16, xl: 24, headingFamily: "serif" }; selects system serif for headings. Actual fonts and glyph metrics vary by platform. No arguments. Ownership: owns the supplied string; reading does not mutate the receiver.

std:ui.name: ReactiveBoolean
std:ui.documentation:
Compiler-generated boolean predicate used by state-reading disabled/readOnly/hidden TSRX expressions. It has no constructor arguments and evaluates after application handlers. <Input readOnly={locked.get()}/> follows the signal without a public lifetime helper. The predicate returns boolean or throws; errors stop the mounted tree and release it. Ownership: stores an owned callback with non-retaining state captures.

```tsrx
const busy = signal(false);
<Button disabled={busy.get()}>Save</Button> // disabled follows busy
```

evaluate.documentation: Evaluates the retained condition with no arguments and returns boolean. The mounted tree reevaluates it after handlers. Example: disabled={count.get() < 5} is true at 0 and false at 5. Captured state-read failures propagate through normal UI error cleanup. Conditions must not mutate state. Ownership: the subtree owns this callback and releases it before its state owners.

std:ui.name: ElementProps
std:ui.documentation:
Checked element identity and accessible naming. Props are ordinary owned records; optional fields have the documented defaults. Use exact quoted names in ordinary records, for example {'aria-label': 'Account'}, and aria-label="Account" in TSRX. Unsupported semantics fail explicitly. Ownership: component calls consume their props and owned descendants.

```tsrx

```

id.documentation: Optional document identifier, without ASCII whitespace or control characters. Defaults to none. <View id="account" /> produces id="account" in HTML. Both adapters retain it as tree metadata; no lookup or routing API is created. Construction throws for invalid IDs. Ownership: consumes the supplied string.

aria-label.documentation: Optional constant or live accessible name; undefined uses visible text or descendants. <Button aria-label={busy.get() ? "Saving" : "Save"}>Save</Button> updates the retained control after handlers without changing its visible label. Regions require a nonblank name; generic text/containers and presentation reject nonempty names. No method arguments. Ownership: transfers the string or evaluator once; captured component state remains non-retaining.

aria-hidden.documentation: Optional constant or live boolean, default false. <Text aria-hidden={decorative.get()}>Decoration</Text> stays painted while leaving accessibility when true. Undefined restores false. Enabled controls in a hidden subtree reject, including after refresh; hiding does not disable controls or remove their layout. Handler errors stop the mounted tree with normal cleanup. Ownership: transfers its evaluator once without retaining state owners.

data-slot.documentation: Optional component slot name, using only ASCII letters, digits and hyphens. Defaults to none. <View data-slot="card-content" /> emits that HTML attribute and retains the same native metadata. Invalid names throw. Checked data/descendant/group selectors can match this metadata; arbitrary CSS selectors remain unsupported. Ownership: consumes the slot string.

data-size.documentation: Optional component size metadata using ASCII letters, digits and hyphens; defaults to absent. <View data-size="sm" className="data-[size=sm]:p-3" /> uses the small metadata condition on both targets. aria-describedby.documentation: Optional constant or live space-separated document IDs; undefined or empty removes the relationship. <Input aria-describedby={invalid.get() ? "error" : "hint"}/> exposes the current referenced text as its accessible description on both targets. Missing IDs are ignored and order is preserved. This does not name the control or run validation. Control characters other than ASCII whitespace reject. Ownership: transfers the ID string or evaluator once; state captures remain weak.

No validation runs and the field value stays unchanged. Both adapters refresh the same retained control after handlers. Ownership: transfers the flag or evaluator once without retaining component state owners.

data-variant.documentation: Optional variant metadata, default absent. ASCII letters, digits and hyphens are accepted; empty omits the attribute. This does not choose styles or change accessibility by itself. Example: <View data-variant="destructive" className="data-[variant=destructive]:text-destructive" /> selects the destructive text token on both targets. Invalid characters throw. Plain string props remain construction-time snapshots. Direct state-reading intrinsic TSRX expressions update after handlers without remounting. Custom components need an explicit reactive prop contract; precomputed values remain snapshots. Ownership: transfers one string or owned evaluator once; bindings do not retain component state owners.

std:ui.documentation:
Checked UI component properties. Props are ordinary owned records; optional fields have the documented defaults. Use exact quoted names in ordinary records, for example {'aria-label': 'Account'}, and aria-label="Account" in TSRX. Unsupported semantics fail explicitly. Classes and Variant default to string, preserving construction-time wrapper contracts. A component author may select ReactiveValue<string> for these type arguments and read those values with useProp(). Ownership: component calls consume their props and owned descendants.

```tsrx
<View as="section" className="grid grid-cols-2 gap-4" aria-label="Stats"><Text>A</Text><Text>B</Text></View>
```

onVisibilityChange.documentation: Optional owned reusable callback (visible: boolean) => void, default none. Reports initial visibility after mounting and each boolean transition after layout, scrolling, resizing or hidden changes. true means this View has positive rectangular area inside the viewport and all clipping ancestors; zero-size or hidden views report false. It does not detect occlusion by siblings, opacity or other windows. Example: const entered = signal(false); return <View onVisibilityChange={(visible) => { if (visible) { entered.set(true); } }}><Text>{entered.get() ? "Ready" : "Waiting"}</Text></View>; shows Ready on first entry and retains it. Callbacks may update state; updates refresh after the callback without intercepting scrolling. Throwing stops the mounted tree with normal cleanup. Keep layout feedback stable: callbacks which repeatedly hide/show their own view can oscillate. Reports follow layout. Static document() serialization never invokes callbacks. Ownership: the View owns the callback; local component state captures are non-retaining and removed nodes receive no late notifications.

onKeyDown.documentation: Optional owned reusable callback (event: KeyboardEvent) => void. Runs for each key press, including auto-repeats, while this View or a descendant has keyboard focus. Give the View tabIndex={0} to make it focusable itself; text fields inside still receive their typing and the handler observes it too. Example: <View tabIndex={0} onKeyDown={(event) => { if (event.key === 'escape') { close(); } }}>…</View>. Ownership: the View owns the callback.

onKeyUp.documentation: Optional owned reusable callback (event: KeyboardEvent) => void. Runs when a key is released while this View or a descendant has keyboard focus. repeat is always false. Example: <View tabIndex={0} onKeyUp={(event) => { if (event.key === 'space') { charging.set(false); } }}/>. Ownership: the View owns the callback.

onPointerDown.documentation: Optional owned reusable callback (event: PointerEvent) => void. Runs when any pointer button is pressed over this View; button says which. Example: <View onPointerDown={(event) => { dragging.set(event.button === 'left'); }}/>. Ownership: the View owns the callback.

onPointerUp.documentation: Optional owned reusable callback (event: PointerEvent) => void. Runs when any pointer button is released over this View. A release outside the View is not reported. Ownership: the View owns the callback.

onPointerMove.documentation: Optional owned reusable callback (event: PointerEvent) => void. Runs as the pointer moves over this View; button is none, or the held button while dragging. clickCount is 0. Keep the handler cheap: it can run every frame. Ownership: the View owns the callback.

onWheel.documentation: Optional owned reusable callback (event: WheelEvent) => void. Runs for each wheel or trackpad scroll over this View. Scrolling containers still scroll. Example: <View onWheel={(event) => { if (event.ctrlKey) { zoomIn(); } }}/>. Ownership: the View owns the callback.

onDoubleClick.documentation: Optional owned reusable callback (event: PointerEvent) => void. Runs on the second press of a left-button double click over this View, with clickCount 2. Ownership: the View owns the callback.

onContextMenu.documentation: Optional owned reusable callback (event: PointerEvent) => void. Runs when the right button is pressed over this View, where a context menu would open; use x and y to place one. For a ready-made menu use ContextMenu. Ownership: the View owns the callback.

onHover.documentation: Optional owned reusable callback (hovered: boolean) => void. Called with true when the pointer enters this View and false when it leaves. Ownership: the View owns the callback.

onFocus.documentation: Optional owned reusable callback () => void. Runs when keyboard focus moves into this View or one of its descendants from outside it. Requires tabIndex; Views without it never report focus. Ownership: the View owns the callback.

onBlur.documentation: Optional owned reusable callback () => void. Runs when keyboard focus leaves this View and all its descendants. Requires tabIndex. Ownership: the View owns the callback.

std:ui.name: Child
std:ui.signature: type Child = string | int | number | TextBinding | Signal<int> | Signal<number> | Signal<boolean> | Signal<string> | Node | null | undefined
std:ui.documentation:
One child of `View` or `Button`: text, a number, a scalar signal, a live expression or a Node.

- Adjacent text and signals form one run of text; `null`, `undefined` and empty strings add nothing.
- Expressions that read component state update after each handler.
- A ternary that reads component state builds only the chosen branch; use `null` for the empty side.
- `Button` accepts only inline content.

Ownership: Nodes and strings move once; signal bindings do not keep state alive.

```tsrx
const count = signal(2);
<Text>{'Items: '}{count}{' total'}</Text> // Items: 2 total
```

std:ui.name: Input

parameters.label: props: InputProps<ReactiveValue<string>, ReactiveValue<string>>
parameters.documentation: Owned text-control options; optional fields use the documented defaults.

std:ui.documentation:
A single-line text field. Leave `value` unset for a field that edits itself (`defaultValue` sets the start), or pass `value` with `onChange` to control it.

- `type="password"` masks input with a reveal toggle; `email`, `url`, `tel` and `search` choose the keyboard and autofill.
- Formatting: `mask` (`9` optional digit, `#` digit, `A` letter), `thousandsSeparator`/`fractionDigits`, or a `pattern` regular expression.
- Events: `onChange`, `onFocus`, `onBlur`, `onSubmit` (Enter).
- Give it an `id` to drive it with `controlInput` and `readInput`.

```tsrx
const email = signal('');
<Input type="email" placeholder="Email" cleanable={true} value={email} onChange={(event) => { email.set(event.target.value); }} onSubmit={() => { save(); }} />
```

Ownership: consumes props, the change callback and non-retaining state bindings; the returned Node owns the field.

std:ui.name: Textarea

parameters.label: props: TextareaProps<ReactiveValue<string>, ReactiveValue<string>>
parameters.documentation: Owned text-control options; optional fields use the documented defaults.

std:ui.documentation:
A multi-line text field with the same value, events and `id` support as `Input`.

`rows` sets a fixed height (default 4); `minRows` and `maxRows` grow with the content, then scroll. `softWrap={false}` scrolls long lines instead of wrapping; `searchable` adds find and replace. Enter inserts a newline unless `submitOnEnter` is true.

```tsrx
<Textarea minRows={2} maxRows={6} placeholder="Write a message" value={draft} onChange={(event) => { draft.set(event.target.value); }} />
```

Ownership: consumes props, the change callback and non-retaining state bindings; the returned Node owns the field.

std:ui.name: InputValue
std:ui.signature: type InputValue = string | int | number | Signal<string> | Signal<int> | Signal<number> | ReactiveInputValue
std:ui.documentation:
Accepted controlled field values. Integers preserve all 64 bits, numbers use ordinary number formatting and strings remain Unicode text. No function arguments. `value={9007199254740993}` displays exactly 9007199254740993. Editing returns strings without numeric parsing. Boolean, nullable and resource payloads are unsupported. Ownership: consumes scalar values or non-retaining bindings; application state remains owned by the returned component tree.

```tsrx
const quantity = signal(1);
<Input value={quantity.get()}/> // shows 1; int, number and string values are accepted
```

std:ui.name: ReactiveInputValue
std:ui.documentation:
Compiler-generated value getter used by state-reading TSRX value expressions. No public helper call is needed. `<Input value={name.get() + '!'}/>` displays the current name followed by ! after each handler. Input bindings require string, int or number; thrown getters stop and dispose the tree. Ownership: owns the getter callback with non-retaining state captures.

```tsrx
const name = signal('Ada');
<Input value={name.get()}/> // the field shows the latest name
```

evaluate.documentation: Owned zero-argument getter returning string | int | number without mutating the binding. Compiler-generated `value={name.get()}` reads the current string. Input supports string/int/number results only; errors propagate to control construction/refresh and dispose the tree. Ownership: callback captures state non-retainingly.

std:ui.name: InputTarget
std:ui.documentation:
Read-only control snapshot observed during onChange. No constructor or function arguments. `event.target.value` is the new normalized text, not parsed data or an element reference. Snapshot contains value, name and id. Ownership: handler borrows the snapshot; explicit clones or Signal.set retain copied data.

```tsrx
<Input onChange={(event) => { console.log(event.target.value); }}/>
```

value.documentation: Normalized committed Unicode field text. Input removes CR/LF; Textarea normalizes CRLF/CR to LF. `event.target.value` is Ada after typing Ada. No numeric parsing, arguments or receiver mutation. Ownership: borrowed snapshot string; copy before retaining.

name.documentation: The field name or empty string when omitted. For <Input name="profile"/>, event.target.name is profile. No arguments or mutation. Ownership: borrowed snapshot string.

id.documentation: The explicit document ID or empty string when omitted. For <Input id="name"/>, event.target.id is name. No arguments or mutation. Ownership: borrowed snapshot string.

std:ui.name: InputChangeEvent
std:ui.documentation:
Committed text-change snapshot passed to onChange. No function arguments. `event.target.value` and `event.currentTarget.value` both contain the normalized new text. No element references, preventDefault or composition methods are available. A callback returns void and may throw; errors stop the mounted tree. Ownership: borrowed only during callback execution.

```tsrx
<Input onChange={(event) => { query.set(clone(event.currentTarget.value)); }}/>
```

target.documentation: Read-only InputTarget snapshot with value, name and id. Direct handlers observe identical target/currentTarget values. `event.target.value` is Ada after a committed Ada edit. No function arguments or receiver mutation. Ownership: borrow lasts for the callback; copy strings to retain them.

currentTarget.documentation: Read-only InputTarget snapshot with value, name and id. Direct handlers observe identical target/currentTarget values. `event.currentTarget.value` is Ada after a committed Ada edit. No function arguments or receiver mutation. Ownership: borrow lasts for the callback; copy strings to retain them.

std:ui.name: TextChild
std:ui.signature: type TextChild = string | int | number | TextBinding | Signal<int> | Signal<number> | Signal<boolean> | Signal<string> | null | undefined
std:ui.documentation:
One child of `Text`: a string, number, scalar signal or live expression.

`null` and `undefined` add nothing, so `<Text>A{null}B</Text>` shows `AB`. Bare booleans and Nodes are not text children. Expressions that read component state update after each handler.

Ownership: strings move once; signal bindings do not keep state alive.

```tsrx
const total = signal(3);
<Text>Total {total}</Text>
```

std:ui.name: TextBinding
std:ui.documentation:
Live text that TSRX creates for an expression reading component state, such as `{count.get() + 1}`.

It refreshes after each handler without rerunning the component. The expression must have no side effects; an error in it stops the window with its message. There is no constructor: TSRX makes these for you.

Ownership: moves once with its getter; it cannot be cloned or sent to threads.

```tsrx
<Text>{t('title')}</Text> // t returns a live TextBinding
```

std:ui.name: Reactive
std:ui.documentation:
A zero-argument getter for a live prop value. TSRX creates one when a prop declared as `ReactiveValue<T>` receives an expression that reads component state.

Read it in the component through `useProp(props.name)`. The getter must not change state or do I/O.

Ownership: owns one getter; it does not keep component state alive.

```tsrx
const ready = signal(true);
<Switch checked={ready.get()}/> // TSRX wraps ready.get() as a Reactive<boolean>
```

evaluate.documentation: Called without arguments to read the latest T. Throws propagate through ordinary UI cleanup. For example, {evaluate: () => count.get() + 1} yields 2 when count is 1. Evaluators must not mutate state. Ownership: owns a reusable callback; moving the descriptor transfers it once.

std:ui.name: ReactiveValue
Computed
std:ui.documentation:
A read-only value computed from other state, created by `computed` or `useProp`.

`get()` evaluates it on every read (no caching, no setter). Results are scalars: numbers, strings, booleans, enums, literal unions or nullable scalars.

Ownership: the component tree owns it; bindings do not keep it alive. It cannot be cloned or sent to threads.

```tsrx
const count = signal(2);
const doubled = computed(() => count.get() * 2);
<Text>{doubled.get()}</Text> // 4
```

std:ui.name: computed
std:ui.documentation:
Creates a read-only value from a getter, re-evaluated on every `get()`.

Example: `const total = computed<int>(() => count.get() + 1)` reads 5 when `count` is 4. Results must be scalars; the getter must not change state or do I/O. An error in the getter, or a disposed signal, throws `UiError` on read. Declare it with `const` in the component, not inside a handler.

Ownership: the component tree owns it; bindings do not keep it alive.

```tsrx
const first = signal('Ada');
const greeting = computed(() => `Hello, ${first.get()}`);
<Text>{greeting.get()}</Text> // Hello, Ada
```

parameters.label: source: Owned<Function<T>>
parameters.documentation: Required reusable zero-argument getter returning a supported scalar T or throwing. No default. Keep reads free of mutation and I/O.

std:ui.name: ViewRenderProps
std:ui.documentation:
Owned View props passed once into a replacement render factory. Contains children, metadata, visibility and styling, without another render field. For example, render={(props) => <View {...props} as="section"/>} creates one section with forwarded children and behavior. Forward needed props into the returned node. Styling/variant fields may be live descriptors; use useProp() when deriving new classes, or forward them intact. Ownership: moves owned children and callbacks once; no wrapper is retained.

```tsrx
<View className={dark.get() ? 'bg-black text-white' : 'bg-white'}><Text>Theme</Text></View>
```

onVisibilityChange.documentation: Optional owned reusable callback (visible: boolean) => void, default none. Reports initial visibility after mounting and each boolean transition after layout, scrolling, resizing or hidden changes. true means this View has positive rectangular area inside the viewport and all clipping ancestors; zero-size or hidden views report false. It does not detect occlusion by siblings, opacity or other windows. Example: const entered = signal(false); return <View onVisibilityChange={(visible) => { if (visible) { entered.set(true); } }}><Text>{entered.get() ? "Ready" : "Waiting"}</Text></View>; shows Ready on first entry and retains it. Callbacks may update state; updates refresh after the callback without intercepting scrolling. Throwing stops the mounted tree with normal cleanup. Keep layout feedback stable: callbacks which repeatedly hide/show their own view can oscillate. Reports follow layout. Static document() serialization never invokes callbacks. Ownership: the View owns the callback; local component state captures are non-retaining and removed nodes receive no late notifications.

onKeyDown.documentation: Optional owned reusable callback (event: KeyboardEvent) => void. Runs for each key press, including auto-repeats, while this View or a descendant has keyboard focus. Give the View tabIndex={0} to make it focusable itself; text fields inside still receive their typing and the handler observes it too. Example: <View tabIndex={0} onKeyDown={(event) => { if (event.key === 'escape') { close(); } }}>…</View>. Ownership: the View owns the callback.

onKeyUp.documentation: Optional owned reusable callback (event: KeyboardEvent) => void. Runs when a key is released while this View or a descendant has keyboard focus. repeat is always false. Example: <View tabIndex={0} onKeyUp={(event) => { if (event.key === 'space') { charging.set(false); } }}/>. Ownership: the View owns the callback.

onPointerDown.documentation: Optional owned reusable callback (event: PointerEvent) => void. Runs when any pointer button is pressed over this View; button says which. Example: <View onPointerDown={(event) => { dragging.set(event.button === 'left'); }}/>. Ownership: the View owns the callback.

onPointerUp.documentation: Optional owned reusable callback (event: PointerEvent) => void. Runs when any pointer button is released over this View. A release outside the View is not reported. Ownership: the View owns the callback.

onPointerMove.documentation: Optional owned reusable callback (event: PointerEvent) => void. Runs as the pointer moves over this View; button is none, or the held button while dragging. clickCount is 0. Keep the handler cheap: it can run every frame. Ownership: the View owns the callback.

onWheel.documentation: Optional owned reusable callback (event: WheelEvent) => void. Runs for each wheel or trackpad scroll over this View. Scrolling containers still scroll. Example: <View onWheel={(event) => { if (event.ctrlKey) { zoomIn(); } }}/>. Ownership: the View owns the callback.

onDoubleClick.documentation: Optional owned reusable callback (event: PointerEvent) => void. Runs on the second press of a left-button double click over this View, with clickCount 2. Ownership: the View owns the callback.

onContextMenu.documentation: Optional owned reusable callback (event: PointerEvent) => void. Runs when the right button is pressed over this View, where a context menu would open; use x and y to place one. For a ready-made menu use ContextMenu. Ownership: the View owns the callback.

onHover.documentation: Optional owned reusable callback (hovered: boolean) => void. Called with true when the pointer enters this View and false when it leaves. Ownership: the View owns the callback.

onFocus.documentation: Optional owned reusable callback () => void. Runs when keyboard focus moves into this View or one of its descendants from outside it. Requires tabIndex; Views without it never report focus. Ownership: the View owns the callback.

onBlur.documentation: Optional owned reusable callback () => void. Runs when keyboard focus leaves this View and all its descendants. Requires tabIndex. Ownership: the View owns the callback.

onFileDrop.documentation: Optional owned reusable callback (paths: string[]) => void. Receives the absolute paths of files and folders dropped onto this View from the system file manager. Example: <View onFileDrop={(paths) => { open(paths[0]); }}>Drop a file</View>. Ownership: the View owns the callback; paths are a read-only copy.

id.documentation: Optional document identifier, without ASCII whitespace or control characters. Defaults to none. <View id="account" /> produces id="account" in HTML. Both adapters retain it as tree metadata; no lookup or routing API is created. Construction throws for invalid IDs. Ownership: consumes the supplied string.

aria-label.documentation: Optional constant or live accessible name; undefined uses visible text or descendants. <Button aria-label={busy.get() ? "Saving" : "Save"}>Save</Button> updates the retained control after handlers without changing its visible label. Regions require a nonblank name; generic text/containers and presentation reject nonempty names. No method arguments. Ownership: transfers the string or evaluator once; captured component state remains non-retaining.

aria-hidden.documentation: Optional constant or live boolean, default false. <Text aria-hidden={decorative.get()}>Decoration</Text> stays painted while leaving accessibility when true. Undefined restores false. Enabled controls in a hidden subtree reject, including after refresh; hiding does not disable controls or remove their layout. Handler errors stop the mounted tree with normal cleanup. Ownership: transfers its evaluator once without retaining state owners.

data-slot.documentation: Optional component slot name, using only ASCII letters, digits and hyphens. Defaults to none. <View data-slot="card-content" /> emits that HTML attribute and retains the same native metadata. Invalid names throw. Checked data/descendant/group selectors can match this metadata; arbitrary CSS selectors remain unsupported. Ownership: consumes the slot string.

role.documentation: Optional noninteractive role: alert, status, separator, group, note, region, none or presentation. Defaults to the chosen tag's implicit role. <Text role="status">Saved</Text> exposes a polite live status; alert is assertive. Region requires aria-label. Separator requires empty text and no children. Unsupported roles throw; role does not turn a View into an interactive widget. Ownership: consumes the role string.

aria-orientation.documentation: Optional separator orientation: horizontal (default) or vertical. Only valid with role="separator". <View role="separator" aria-orientation="vertical" /> exposes a vertical, nonfocusable separator on both backends. This describes orientation; classes still control dimensions. Other roles/values throw. Ownership: consumes the string.

as.documentation: Optional semantic container tag: div (default), section, span, label, kbd or code. <View as="kbd" className="inline-flex flex-row gap-1">Ctrl<Text>+</Text>K</View> composes keyboard text while retaining normal child ownership. kbd/code are noninteractive phrasing containers; they can compose inside Button, but an interactive descendant still rejects there. Generic container layout remains flex column unless classes override it. Tags do not register keyboard handlers. Unknown tags throw. Ownership: consumes the tag and child subtrees. Table parts include table, thead, tbody, tfoot, caption, tr, th and td. Semantic tags alone preserve explicit layout; table/table-row/table-cell display utilities opt into shared-column layout. Caption and footer retain their native roles.

children.documentation:
Optional ordered Child array; omission defaults to empty. Strings, exact ints, numbers, direct scalar Signal bindings and compiler-retained scalar expressions display in order. Null/undefined contribute no characters or placeholder. View accepts owned subtrees; Button requires noninteractive phrasing content. <Text>{count.get()+1}</Text> updates after handlers for directly declared component state. Top-level/imported helpers with declared scalar returns participate. Precomputed values, unknown/inferred helpers, arbitrary prop-record reads remain snapshots. Bare booleans are unsupported; boolean Signal bindings display true/false. Getter expressions must be pure; application errors propagate.  A conditional TSRX ternary whose condition reads directly declared component state mounts only its selected branch. Nested branches work. Unchanged selection preserves child state; removal releases it once, and later selection constructs fresh state. Transparent slots add no layout or accessibility element. Empty/absent derived text in containers also contributes no anonymous layout item; explicit Text components keep their own node. For example, <View>{visible.get()?<Text>Ready</Text>:null}</View> shows/hides Ready. Prebuilt owned Nodes cannot be consumed repeatedly from captures; ordinary callback ownership errors apply. Invalid interactive/label/hidden ancestry is checked again after replacement. Pass content between tags or through children={values}; combining both is rejected. Explicit child arrays transfer once and remain subject to ordinary ownership checks.

Ownership: consumes strings and owned children once; bindings do not retain state owners and owning child arrays cannot be cloned.

className.documentation: Optional shared utility string, default empty. <View className="flex-row gap-4" /> uses a horizontal container and project spacing.md between children. Later classes override earlier properties within each state; unknown utilities throw. Grid/flex display, equal grid tracks (1–12), bounded grid placement, per-side padding/gaps, preferred/min/max dimensions, alignment, wrapping and grow/shrink use the same logical-pixel model on both targets. p/px/py and size expand to independent properties; later classes win per property/state. Spacing 2/4/6 uses sm/md/lg, 1 uses sm/2, 3 averages sm/md; other numeric sizes use spacing.md/4 per unit. Percentage heights need a definite parent height. Example: <View className="grid grid-cols-2 gap-4 p-4" /> creates two equal tracks with default 16px gaps/padding. Viewport sm/md/lg/xl/2xl variants use 640/768/1024/1280/1536 logical pixels. hidden removes the retained subtree from layout, paint, keyboard/pointer interaction and accessibility. hidden lg:flex shows it from 1024 logical pixels; state and handler ownership stay intact while hidden. Arbitrary CSS, container queries, named grid lines and subgrid remain unsupported. Semantic color utilities accept /N alpha multiplication for integer percentages 0–100 and transparent. ring-0/1/2/3 sets an outer surface ring width; ring-COLOR selects its color. These rings do not change layout and remain independent of the focus outline. Example: ring-1 ring-foreground/10 draws a 1px surface ring at 10% token alpha. Unsupported percentages throw. Native paint uses 8-bit sRGB; original theme strings are preserved. Scoped spacing uses [--NAME:--spacing(N)] and p/gap-(--NAME), inheriting numeric logical pixels. Missing variables resolve to zero. Metadata declarations are supported; interaction-state declarations and arbitrary expressions are rejected. Border sides and corners merge independently, overflow-hidden clips paint and pointer targets, and generic font/weight/line-height utilities are shared. aspect-square/video/[W/H]/[R]/auto sets or clears a preferred width/height ratio, normalized to finite positive f32 layout precision on both targets. A definite width derives automatic height; explicit dimensions and min/max constraints win. Zero, negative, nonfinite and native range overflow/underflow reject. Example: <View className="w-64 aspect-video"/> is 256 by 144 logical pixels at default spacing. Every UI layout box establishes a containing block. absolute removes a box from normal flow and positions it in its immediate UI parent; relative keeps normal flow. top/right/bottom/left and inset/inset-x/inset-y use theme spacing, percentages or auto, with optional negative numeric/fraction offsets. Later classes win per side. Inline descendants reject box utilities. fixed, sticky, z-index and transforms remain unsupported. Example: <View className="w-64 h-32"><View className="absolute top-2 right-2 w-8 h-8" /></View> places the child 8px from the top and right at default spacing. Direct state-reading intrinsic TSRX expressions update after handlers without remounting. Custom components need an explicit reactive prop contract; precomputed values remain snapshots. Ownership: transfers one string or owned evaluator once; bindings do not retain component state owners. Text flow supports whitespace-normal/nowrap/pre/pre-wrap; nowrap collapses spaces without soft wraps. underline/no-underline controls local decoration, and underline-offset-auto/0/1/2/4/8 selects font metrics or logical pixels below the baseline. Ancestor decorations remain. rounded-2xl/3xl/4xl uses 1.25/1.5/2 times radius.xl, with lg fallback. [a]: variants apply only to a Link. Stored text and editable values remain unchanged.

data-size.documentation: Optional component size metadata using ASCII letters, digits and hyphens; defaults to absent. <View data-size="sm" className="data-[size=sm]:p-3" /> uses the small metadata condition on both targets. The string does not select dimensions by itself or add an accessibility role. Invalid characters throw. No function arguments. Ownership: consumes the supplied string.

aria-describedby.documentation: Optional constant or live space-separated document IDs; undefined or empty removes the relationship. <Input aria-describedby={invalid.get() ? "error" : "hint"}/> exposes the current referenced text as its accessible description on both targets. Missing IDs are ignored and order is preserved. aria-invalid.documentation: Optional constant or live boolean describing validation state. <Input aria-invalid={invalid.get() ? true : undefined}/> adds invalid styling and accessibility when true; undefined removes the explicit state and false states valid. No validation runs and the field value stays unchanged. Both adapters refresh the same retained control after handlers. Ownership: transfers the flag or evaluator once without retaining component state owners.

htmlFor.documentation: Optional associated control ID, valid only with as="label". <View as="label" htmlFor="name">Name</View> labels and focuses the control id="name" on both targets. Omit htmlFor to label the first enclosed control. Nested labels and multiple enclosed controls throw. Invalid ID whitespace/control characters throw. Ownership: copies the index; retains no focus handle.

data-variant.documentation: Optional variant metadata, default absent. ASCII letters, digits and hyphens are accepted; empty omits the attribute. This does not choose styles or change accessibility by itself. Example: <View data-variant="destructive" className="data-[variant=destructive]:text-destructive" /> selects the destructive text token on both targets. Invalid characters throw. Plain string props remain construction-time snapshots. Direct state-reading intrinsic TSRX expressions update after handlers without remounting. Custom components need an explicit reactive prop contract; precomputed values remain snapshots. Ownership: transfers one string or owned evaluator once; bindings do not retain component state owners.

colSpan.documentation: Optional construction-time integer from 1 through 1000; omission spans one column. Only as="th" or as="td" accepts it. Invalid values throw instead of silently clamping. Example: <View as="td" colSpan={2}>Total</View> covers two table columns. Row spans are unsupported. No receiver mutation or ownership change.

scope.documentation: Optional table header association: row, col, rowgroup or colgroup. Only as="th" accepts it; omission lets the target infer association. Example: <View as="th" scope="row">Invoice</View> exposes a row header. Invalid tags/values throw. Ownership: transfers the string once.

data-state.documentation: Optional constant or live styling state. ASCII letters, digits and hyphens are accepted; empty or undefined removes it. Does not set accessibility selection. Example: <View data-state={selected.get() ? "selected" : undefined} className="data-[state=selected]:bg-muted"/> updates the retained background after handlers. Invalid values throw with normal cleanup. Custom wrappers preserve the ReactiveValue contract. Ownership: transfers the string or evaluator once; captures do not retain state owners.

std:ui.name: useId
std:ui.documentation:
Returns a new unique ID string for this run of the program, such as for pairing a label with a field.

Each call returns a different ID; keep the one you get while building the component. IDs are not stable across runs and are not secrets.

Ownership: returns an owned string; clone it to use it in more than one prop.

```tsrx
const id = useId();
<Label text="Email"/>
<Input id={id} aria-label="Email"/>
```

std:ui.name: useProp

parameters.label: source: ReactiveValue<T>
parameters.documentation: Required scalar constant or TSRX reactive descriptor; no default. Use ?? before adapting an optional field when it needs a default.

std:ui.name: notify

parameters.label: message: string
parameters.documentation: Body text.

parameters.label: options?: NotifyOptions
parameters.documentation: Title, variant (info, success, warning, error) and delivery (app, system, both).

std:ui.documentation:
Shows a toast notification in the active window.

Options: `title`, `variant` (`info`, `success`, `warning`, `error`), `delivery` (`app`, `system` or `both`), `id` (a later toast with the same id replaces it; `dismissNotification(id)` removes it), `icon`, `placement`, `autohide` (default true unless there is an `action`), `action` (a button label) and `onEvent`, called once with `'action'`, `'click'` or `'close'`.

```tsrx
notify('File deleted', { variant: 'warning', id: 'delete', action: 'Undo', onEvent: (event) => { if (event === 'action') { restore(); } } });
```

Ownership: arguments are read; nothing is retained after the call except an owned callback, which runs once.

std:ui.name: NotifyOptions
std:ui.documentation:
Options for notify: title, variant, delivery, id, icon, placement, autohide, action and onEvent.

```tsrx
notify('Saved', { variant: 'success', placement: 'bottom-right' });
```

std:ui.name: setWindowTitle

parameters.label: title: string
parameters.documentation: New title.

std:ui.documentation:
Sets the active window's title on the next frame.

```tsrx
setWindowTitle(`Editing ${name.get()}`);
```

Ownership: arguments are read; nothing is retained after the call except an owned callback, which runs once.

std:ui.name: minimizeWindow
std:ui.documentation:
Minimizes the active window on the next frame.

```tsrx
<Button onPress={() => { minimizeWindow(); }}>Minimize</Button>
```

std:ui.name: zoomWindow
std:ui.documentation:
Toggles the active window between its normal and zoomed (maximized) size on the next frame.

```tsrx
<Button onPress={() => { zoomWindow(); }}>Zoom</Button>
```

std:ui.name: zoomIn
std:ui.documentation:
Zooms the whole interface one step larger, up to 300%.

Zoom scales text, spacing and components in every window, on top of the system text-size setting. Steps: 50, 67, 75, 80, 90, 100, 110, 125, 150, 175, 200, 250, 300%.

```tsrx
<Shortcut command="zoom-in" keys="secondary-=" onTrigger={() => { zoomIn(); }}/>
```

std:ui.name: zoomOut
std:ui.documentation:
Zooms the whole interface one step smaller, down to 50%.

Zoom scales text, spacing and components in every window, on top of the system text-size setting. Steps: 50, 67, 75, 80, 90, 100, 110, 125, 150, 175, 200, 250, 300%.

```tsrx
<Button onPress={() => { zoomOut(); }}>Smaller</Button>
```

std:ui.name: resetZoom
std:ui.documentation:
Returns the interface to 100 percent zoom on the next frame. The system text-size preference still applies.

```tsrx
<Button onPress={() => { resetZoom(); }}>Actual size</Button>
```

std:ui.name: setZoom

parameters.label: level: number
parameters.documentation: Zoom factor where 1 is 100 percent. Clamped to 0.5–3; NaN and infinities are ignored.

std:ui.documentation:
Sets the interface zoom to an exact `level`, for example to restore a saved preference.

Zoom scales text, spacing and components in every window, on top of the system text-size setting. Levels: 50, 67, 75, 80, 90, 100, 110, 125, 150, 175, 200, 250, 300%.

```tsrx
setZoom(1.25); // 125 percent
```

std:ui.name: toggleFullscreen
std:ui.documentation:
Toggles full-screen mode for the active window on the next frame.

```tsrx
<Button onPress={() => { toggleFullscreen(); }}>Full screen</Button>
```

std:ui.name: closeWindow
std:ui.documentation:
Closes the active window on the next frame. The application quits, and run returns Ok, when its last window closes.

```tsrx
<Button onPress={() => { closeWindow(); }}>Close</Button>
```

std:ui.name: quit
std:ui.documentation:
Quits the application on the next frame; run then returns Ok.

```tsrx
<Button onPress={() => { quit(); }}>Quit</Button>
```

std:ui.name: openUrl

parameters.label: url: string
parameters.documentation: URL to open.

std:ui.documentation:
Opens a URL with the system's default handler, such as a browser for https links or a mail client for mailto links.

```tsrx
<Button onPress={() => { openUrl('https://example.com/docs'); }}>Docs</Button>
```

Ownership: arguments are read; nothing is retained after the call except an owned callback, which runs once.

std:ui.name: revealPath

parameters.label: path: string
parameters.documentation: Absolute path to the existing file or directory to show.

std:ui.documentation:
Requests that the desktop file manager reveal the local file or folder at path. Returns immediately. The platform chooses how to present the location.

```tsrx
<Button onPress={() => { revealPath(document.path); }}>Reveal file</Button>
```

Ownership: the request owns its path.

std:ui.name: writeClipboard

parameters.label: text: string
parameters.documentation: Text to copy.

std:ui.documentation:
Copies text to the system clipboard on the next frame. Ownership: arguments are read; nothing is retained after the call except an owned callback, which runs once.

```tsrx
<Button onPress={() => { writeClipboard('https://example.com'); }}>Copy link</Button>
```

std:ui.name: readClipboard

parameters.label: onRead
parameters.documentation: Receives the clipboard text.

std:ui.documentation:
Reads text from the system clipboard and passes it to onRead on the next frame; the text is empty when the clipboard holds no text. Signals set in onRead refresh the window like any handler.

```tsrx
readClipboard((text) => { pasted.set(clone(text)); });
```

Ownership: arguments are read; nothing is retained after the call except an owned callback, which runs once.

std:ui.name: pickFiles
std:ui.signature: pickFiles(onPicked: Owned<Function<void, [paths: ReadOnly<string>]>>, options?: PickFilesOptions): void

parameters.label: onPicked
parameters.documentation: Receives newline-separated paths.

parameters.label: options?: PickFilesOptions
parameters.documentation: multiple and directories, both default false.

std:ui.documentation:

std:ui.name: t

Live translated text with fixed values. It follows setLocale, but its values are read once; for values that read state write translateWith inside TSRX markup. Catalogs are JSON objects, usually imported: `import fr from './locales/fr.json'`. Nested objects make dotted keys (menu.save), {name} placeholders take values, and a numeric count selects key_zero, key_one or key_other (zero falls back to other). std:ui.signature: controlInput(id: string, action: InputAction, options?: InputActionOptions): void

parameters.label: id
parameters.documentation: The id prop of the target Input, Textarea or CodeEditor.

parameters.label: action
parameters.documentation: What to do: focus, selectAll, unselect, clear, insert, replace, setValue, setCursor, setSelection, addSelection, toggleMasked, scrollTo, insertToken, openSearch, openReplace, search, nextMatch, previousMatch, replaceMatch, replaceAllMatches or closeSearch.

std:ui.name: InputSnapshot
std:ui.documentation:

- `key`: lowercase letters and digits, or names such as `enter`, `escape`, `tab`, `space`, `up`, `pageup`, `f1`.

std:ui.name: PointerEvent
std:ui.documentation:
A pointer press, release or move over a View (`onPointerDown`, `onPointerUp`, `onPointerMove`, `onDoubleClick`, `onContextMenu`).

- `button`: `left`, `right`, `middle`, `back`, `forward`, or `none` while moving.

- `ctrlKey`, `altKey`, `shiftKey`, `metaKey` (Command on macOS).

```tsrx

```

Ownership: a read-only copy for the duration of the handler.

std:ui.name: WheelEvent
std:ui.documentation:

`deltaX` and `deltaY` are the distances in `deltaMode` units (`pixel` for trackpads, `line` for notched wheels); positive `deltaY` moves content up. The container still scrolls; the handler only observes. Modifier flags are as in `PointerEvent`.


Ownership: a read-only copy for the duration of the handler.

std:ui.name: controlTerminal
std:ui.signature: controlTerminal(id: string, request: TerminalRequest, onResult: Owned<Function<void, [result: ReadOnly<TerminalCommandResult>]>>): void

parameters.label: id
parameters.documentation: Unique nonempty id of the mounted Terminal in the originating window.

parameters.label: request
parameters.documentation: Action plus text for write/paste or signed 32-bit lines for scroll. close force-terminates jobs; interrupt sends Ctrl+C.

parameters.label: onResult
parameters.documentation: Called once with delivery success or an error. Delivery is not command completion.

std:ui.documentation:
Sends an action to the `Terminal` with this `id`, then calls `onResult` on the next frame.

An unknown id, or no terminal support, gives `ok: false`. `write` sends exact text and `paste` normalizes line endings; input is limited to 1 MiB and runs commands when it ends with Enter. `close` ends the shell without letting programs save. Check your own permissions before sending input.

```tsrx
controlTerminal('shell', {action: 'interrupt'}, (result) => { console.log(result.ok); });
```

Prints true when Ctrl+C was delivered to the mounted session. Ownership: owns request and callback; session stays owned by its mounted node. A mismatched expectedGeneration returns ok=false without applying the action. restart rejects a running shell; select requires four in-grid coordinates and does not focus or send input.

parameters.label: id

parameters.label: onRead
parameters.documentation: Called once with copied visible text, selected text, geometry, status and focus; found=false when no mounted session matches.


Prints true for a previously displayed shell session, including when hidden. Ownership: owns the callback and copied id; callback borrows an independent snapshot.

std:ui.name: SliderProps
std:ui.documentation:
A draggable numeric slider.

Props (all optional):
- `value`: The value (or a range's start), controlled; set it from onChange. Without it the slider keeps its own value.
- `defaultValue`: Initial value when `value` is unset.
- `range`: Two thumbs: value is the start and endValue the end. Read when it mounts.
- `endValue`: A range's end, controlled; set it from onEndChange.
- `defaultEndValue`: A range's initial end.
- `min`: Smallest value. Defaults to 0.
- `max`: Largest value. Defaults to 100.
- `step`: Increment. Defaults to 1.
- `scale`: Value spacing along the track; logarithmic suits volumes and frequencies.
- `vertical`: A vertical track; give it a height.
- `reverse`: Runs from max to min.
- `disabled`: Ignores input.
- `accessibilityLabel`: Names the slider for assistive technology.
- `onChange`: Runs with the value (a range's start) while dragging.
- `onEndChange`: Runs with a range's end while dragging.
- `onCommit`: Runs with the value (a range's start) when the thumb is released.
- `className`: Utility classes. A signal expression updates them live without remounting; unknown utilities throw.

```tsrx
<Slider value={volume.get()} onChange={(value) => { volume.set(value); }} className="w-64"/>
```

Ownership: consumes its props and children; the returned Node owns its handlers.

std:ui.name: TabsProps
std:ui.documentation:
A row of Tab triggers that switches between TabsContent panels. Explicit text-size classes on Tabs or an individual Tab apply to the labels; the height grows to fit larger text.

Props (all optional):
- `value`: The selected tab's value, controlled; set it from onChange. Without it the tabs keep their own selection.
- `defaultValue`: Initially selected tab value when `value` is unset. Defaults to the first tab.
- `variant`: Tab style: tab (default), underline, pill, outline, segmented or folder (browser-style tabs that join the content below).
- `menu`: Adds a menu listing every tab, for bars that overflow.
- `maxWidth`: Most width in pixels before the bar scrolls.
- `size`: Tab size: xsmall, small, medium (default) or large.
- `onChange`: Runs with the clicked tab's value.
- `children`: Tab, TabsContent, TabsPrefix, TabsSuffix and TabsEmptySpace elements.
- `className`: Utility classes. A signal expression updates them live without remounting; unknown utilities throw.

```tsrx
<Tabs defaultValue="account">
  <Tab value="account">Account</Tab>
  <Tab value="password">Password</Tab>
  <TabsContent value="account"><Text>Make changes to your account here.</Text></TabsContent>
  <TabsContent value="password"><Text>Change your password here.</Text></TabsContent>
</Tabs>
```

std:ui.documentation:
Stacked sections that expand and collapse. Each AccordionItem has an AccordionTrigger heading and AccordionContent.

Props (all optional):
- `value`: Open item values, one per line, controlled; set it from onChange. Without it the accordion keeps its own open items.

- `disabled`: Disables every item.
- `size`: Size: xsmall, small, medium (default) or large.
- `onChange`: Runs with the open item values after each toggle.

- `className`: Utility classes. A signal expression updates them live without remounting; unknown utilities throw.

- `maxWidth`: Largest width in pixels.
- `marginTop`: Distance from the top of the window in pixels.

- `cancelText`: Shorthand: draws Kit's Cancel button with this text; onCancel runs when pressed.

- `onClose`: Runs after it closes.
- `onOk`: Runs on Return or confirmation. With a custom footer and no shorthand buttons, set open to false in the handler after validation succeeds.

std:ui.name: DropdownMenuProps
std:ui.documentation:
A button that opens a menu of MenuItem, MenuLabel, MenuSeparator and Submenu children. A Button child, if present, is the trigger with all its options.

Props (all optional):
- `label`: Trigger text when no Button child is given.
- `split`: Show a split button: the main button runs onClick and the arrow opens the menu. Implied by onClick.
- `caret`: Show the dropdown caret on a custom trigger button. A label trigger always shows it.
- `variant`: Trigger look.
- `outline`: Outline trigger.
- `size`: Trigger size.
- `disabled`: Disables the trigger.
- `selected`: Shows the trigger pressed.
- `anchor`: Point of the menu aligned to the trigger. Defaults to top-left.
- `menuLabel`: Name read by screen readers for the menu toggle.
- `color`: Custom trigger fill: a theme color name or #rrggbb.
- `foreground`: Custom trigger text color.
- `hoverColor`: Custom trigger hover fill.
- `activeColor`: Custom trigger pressed fill.
- `minWidth`: Minimum menu width in pixels.
- `maxWidth`: Maximum menu width in pixels.
- `maxHeight`: Maximum menu height in pixels; taller menus scroll.
- `scrollable`: Lets a long menu scroll.
- `checkSide`: Side the check mark of checked items is drawn on. Defaults to left.
- `externalLinkIcon`: Shows an external-link icon on link items. Defaults to true.
- `fontSize`: Popup text size in logical pixels, 8–40. Omission uses native menu defaults. Applies to entries when the popup is opened.
- `onClick`: Runs when the main part of a split button is clicked; makes the button split.
- `children`: MenuItem, MenuLabel, MenuSeparator and Submenu elements.
- `className`: Utility classes. A signal expression updates them live without remounting; unknown utilities throw.

```tsrx
<DropdownMenu label="Actions"><MenuItem label="Duplicate" onSelect={() => { duplicate(); }}/></DropdownMenu>
```

std:ui.name: ListProps
std:ui.documentation:
A virtualized, keyboard-navigable list of ListItem rows, optionally in ListGroup sections with a search field. Give it a height with className.

Props (all optional):
- `searchable`: Shows a search field that filters rows by their text, value and keywords.
- `placeholder`: Hint in the search field.
- `selectable`: false turns off row highlighting and keyboard selection. Defaults to true.
- `selected`: Highlighted row (0-based across all groups), controlled.
- `defaultSelected`: Initially highlighted row when `selected` is unset.
- `loading`: Shows skeleton rows instead of the items.
- `hasMore`: More rows can load; scrolling near the end fires onLoadMore.
- `loadMoreThreshold`: Rows from the end at which onLoadMore fires. Defaults to 20.
- `scrollbarVisible`: false hides the scrollbar. Defaults to true.
- `scrollBounce`: Elastic overscroll at the ends.
- `size`: Row size: xsmall, small, medium (default) or large.
- `query`: The search text, controlled.
- `autoFocus`: Focuses the list (or its search field) when it mounts.
- `scrollResetKey`: Changing this key scrolls to the first row without selecting it. Keep it stable during background updates; use a page/filter identity to reset navigation. No effect on initial selection.
- `minItemWidth`: Shows flat ListItem children as a responsive grid of cards at least this many logical pixels wide. Use selectable=false and onConfirm to activate cards. Omit for an ordinary list.
- `onSelect`: Receives the highlighted row's value (or its index) as the highlight moves.
- `onConfirm`: Receives the row's value (or its index) on click or Enter.
- `onCancel`: Runs when Escape clears the highlight.
- `onLoadMore`: Runs when scrolling nears the end while hasMore is true; append rows and clear hasMore when done.
- `children`: ListItem, ListSeparator, ListGroup and ListEmpty elements.
- `className`: Utility classes. A signal expression updates them live without remounting; unknown utilities throw.

```tsrx
<List className="h-64" searchable={true} onConfirm={(value) => { console.log(value); }}>
  <ListGroup heading="Fruits">
    <ListItem value="apple">Apple</ListItem>
    <ListItem value="banana">Banana</ListItem>
  </ListGroup>
  <ListGroup heading="Vegetables">
    <ListItem value="carrot">Carrot</ListItem>
  </ListGroup>
  <ListEmpty><Text variant="muted">No matches.</Text></ListEmpty>
</List>
```
